title.zh: 卷三十四 列傳第二十四 顏延之 沈懷文 周朗
title.en: Volume 34 Biographies 24: Yan Yanzhi, Shen Huaiwen, Zhou Lang
title.raw: 卷三十四 列傳第二十四 顏延之 沈懷文 周朗 Volume 34 Biographies 24: Yan Yanzhi, Shen Huaiwen, Zhou Lang

sentences.zh: 顏延之

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi

sentences.zh: 顏延之字延年，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi, courtesy name Yannian, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi, styled Yannian, came from Linyi in Langye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖含，晉右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Han served as Right Director of Splendid Honors in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Han had been Right Director of Splendid Honors under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖約，零陵太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Administrator of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue served as administrator of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 父顒，護軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Yong was a staff officer to the Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong held a staff post under the Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 延之少孤貧，居負郭，好讀書，無所不覽，文章冠絕當時。

translations.literal: Yanzhi lost his father young and lived in poverty on the outskirts of the city; he loved reading and perused everything, and his writing surpassed all of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, Yanzhi lived just outside the city walls. He read voraciously in every field, and his prose stood above that of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，不護細行。

translations.literal: He loved wine and did not guard small conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily and cared little for propriety in small matters.

sentences.zh: 年三十猶未昏。

translations.literal: At thirty he had still not married.
translations.idiomatic: He remained unmarried until he was thirty.

sentences.zh: 妹適東莞劉穆之子憲之。

translations.literal: His younger sister married Xianzhi, son of Liu Mu of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: A younger sister of his married Xianzhi, son of Liu Mu of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 穆之聞其美才，將仕之，先欲相見，延之不往也。

translations.literal: Mu heard of his fine talent and meant to employ him, and first wished to meet him; Yanzhi would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mu, hearing of his gifts, wished to take him into service and asked to meet him first. Yanzhi refused to come.

sentences.zh: 後為宋武帝豫章公世子中軍行參軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Army Aide to the Heir Apparent's Central Army under Duke of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became an aide in the heir apparent's central army under the Duke of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 及武帝北伐，有宋公之授，府遣延之慶殊命。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu marched north, the office was ordered to send Yanzhi to celebrate the extraordinary appointment as Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched north and received the title Duke of Song, the staff dispatched Yanzhi to compose a celebratory address.

sentences.zh: 行至洛陽，周視故宮室，盡為禾黍，淒然詠黍離篇。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, he toured the old palaces, all turned to millet and sorghum, and sadly chanted the 'Millet' ode.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he walked the ruined palaces, now fields of millet and sorghum, and mournfully recited the 'Millet' ode.

sentences.zh: 道中作詩二首，為謝晦、傅亮所賞。

translations.literal: On the road he composed two poems, which Xie Hui and Fu Liang admired.
translations.idiomatic: En route he wrote two poems that won praise from Xie Hui and Fu Liang.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，補太子舍人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu received the Mandate, Yanzhi was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu accepted the throne, Yanzhi was made an attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 雁門周續之隱廬山，儒學著稱。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuzhi of Yanmen lived in seclusion on Mount Lu and was renowned in Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuzhi of Yanmen, a recluse on Mount Lu, was famed for classical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 永初中，征詣都下，開館以居之。

translations.literal: In the Yongchu era he was summoned to the capital and given a hall in which to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongchu reign he was summoned to court and housed in a lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 武帝親幸，朝彥畢至。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally visited; court worthies all arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person, and the leading men of court gathered.

sentences.zh: 延之宮官列卑，引升上席。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's palace rank was low, yet he was brought up to the upper seats.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yanzhi held a low palace post, he was seated among the honored guests.

sentences.zh: 上使問續之三義，續之雅仗辭辯，延之每以簡要連挫續之。

translations.literal: The emperor had him question Xuzhi on the Three Meanings; Xuzhi relied on eloquent debate, and Yanzhi repeatedly defeated him with brevity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set him to debate Xuzhi on the Three Meanings. Xuzhi leaned on fluent rhetoric; Yanzhi cut him down again and again with terse answers.

sentences.zh: 上又使還自敷釋，言約理暢，莫不稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor also had him expound in turn; his words were few and the reasoning clear, and none failed to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Yanzhi explain the doctrine himself. His speech was spare and lucid, and all praised it.

sentences.zh: 再遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Attendant of the Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to attendant in the central palace.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令傅亮自以文義一時莫及，延之負其才，不為之下，亮甚疾焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Liang considered his literary learning unmatched in the age, yet Yanzhi, trusting in his talent, would not rank below him, and Liang greatly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, Director of the Masters of Writing, believed no one matched him in letters; Yanzhi, sure of his own gifts, refused to defer, and Liang deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王義真待之甚厚，徐羨之等疑延之為同異，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Yizhen treated him very generously; Xu Xianzhi and others suspected Yanzhi of siding with them and were greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yizhen of Luling treated him warmly, but Xu Xianzhi and his faction suspected Yanzhi of divided loyalty and took strong dislike to him.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，累遷始安太守。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Yanzhi was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he rose by stages to administrator of Shian.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍謝晦謂延之曰：「昔荀勖忌阮咸，斥為始平郡，今卿又為始安，可謂'二始'。

translations.literal: General of the Palace Guard Xie Hui said to Yanzhi, "In the past Xun Xu envied Ruan Xian and banished him to Shiping commandery; now you too have been sent to Shian—one might call it the 'two Shi's.'"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, General of the Palace Guard, told him, "Once Xun Xu drove Ruan Xian out to Shiping; now you have been sent to Shian—the 'two beginnings,' as it were."

sentences.zh: 」黃門郎殷景仁亦謂之曰：「所謂人惡俊異，世疵文雅。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Yin Jingren also said to him, "This is what people mean when they say the world hates the outstanding and faults the refined."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren, an attendant gentleman, added, "So the world hates the brilliant and scorns the cultivated."

sentences.zh: 」延之之郡，道經汨潭，為湘州刺史張邵祭屈原文以致其意。

translations.literal: On the way to his commandery Yanzhi passed the Mi Pool and, on behalf of the Inspector of Xiang Province Zhang Shao, offered sacrifice to Qu Yuan's spirit to convey his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: En route to his post he stopped at the Mi Pool and, at the request of Xiang Province inspector Zhang Shao, sacrificed to Qu Yuan to declare his sentiments.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，羨之等誅，徵為中書侍郎，轉太子中庶子，領步兵校尉，賞遇甚厚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, after Xianzhi and the others were executed, Yanzhi was recalled as Gentleman of the Secretariat and transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers, and was richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3, once Xianzhi's faction had fallen, Yanzhi was recalled as a secretariat gentleman, made attendant to the heir apparent and colonel of footsoldiers, and treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 延之既以才學見遇，當時多相推服，唯袁淑年倍小延之，不相推重。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, having been honored for talent and learning, was widely admired, yet only Yuan Shu, though half his age, would not defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: Honored for scholarship, Yanzhi was widely admired—only Yuan Shu, though half his age, refused to yield to him.

sentences.zh: 延之忿於眾中折之曰：「昔陳元方與孔元駿齊年文學，元駿拜元方於床下，今君何得不見拜？

translations.literal: Yanzhi, angry before the assembly, rebuked him, saying, "In the past Chen Yuanfang and Kong Yuanjun were peers in letters; Yuanjun bowed to Yuanfang at the bedside—why should you not bow to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Before the company Yanzhi snapped at him: "Chen Yuanfang and Kong Yuanjun were literary equals in their day, and Yuanjun bowed to Yuanfang at the bedside. Why won't you bow to me?"

sentences.zh: 「淑無以對。

translations.literal: Shu had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had no answer.

sentences.zh: 延之疏誕，不能取容當世，見劉湛、殷景仁專當要任，意有不平。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was blunt and eccentric and could not accommodate himself to the age; seeing Liu Zhan and Yin Jingren monopolize key posts, he felt aggrieved.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and unbending, Yanzhi could not trim himself to the times. Liu Zhan and Yin Jingren held the chief posts, and he resented it.

sentences.zh: 常言：「天下事豈一人之智所能獨了」。

translations.literal: He often said, "Can the affairs of the realm be settled by the wit of one man alone?"
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Surely the empire is not a thing one mind can manage alone."

sentences.zh: 辭意激揚，每犯權要。

translations.literal: His words were heated and he repeatedly offended the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: His language grew fierce, and he repeatedly crossed those in power.

sentences.zh: 又少經為湛父柳後將軍主簿，至是謂湛曰：「吾名器不升，當由作卿家吏耳。

translations.literal: He had once served as chief clerk to Rear General Liu, father of Zhan; now he told Zhan, "My rank never rises—no doubt because I was once your family's clerk."
translations.idiomatic: He had once been chief clerk to Zhan's father, Rear General Liu. Now he told Zhan, "My titles never advance—perhaps because I once served as your family's clerk."

sentences.zh: 」湛恨焉，言于彭城王義康，出為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: Zhan hated this and spoke to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; Yanzhi was sent out as Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan took offense and complained to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng. Yanzhi was exiled to Yongjia as administrator.

sentences.zh: 延之甚怨憤，乃作五君詠，以述竹林七賢，山濤、王戎以貴顯被黜。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was deeply resentful and composed the Five Lord Odes, treating the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove; Shan Tao and Wang Rong were omitted for their lofty rank.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter with rage, he wrote the Five Lord Odes on the Bamboo Grove sages, omitting Shan Tao and Wang Rong for their worldly success.

sentences.zh: 詠嵇康云：「鸞翮有時鎩，龍性誰能馴。

translations.literal: On Ji Kang he wrote: "The phoenix pinion is sometimes clipped; who can tame the nature of a dragon?"
translations.idiomatic: Of Ji Kang he wrote: "Even a phoenix's pinion may be clipped—who can tame a dragon's nature?"

sentences.zh: 」詠阮籍云：「物故不可論，途窮能無慟。

translations.literal: On Ruan Ji he wrote: "When things are gone they cannot be discussed; at the road's end, how can one not grieve?"
translations.idiomatic: Of Ruan Ji: "What is past cannot be argued; at the end of the road, who would not mourn?"

sentences.zh: 」詠阮咸云：「屢薦不入官，一麾乃出守。

translations.literal: On Ruan Xian he wrote: "Repeatedly recommended yet never given office; one wave of the hand and he was sent to guard a district."
translations.idiomatic: Of Ruan Xian: "Recommended again and again, never given office; one gesture, and he was sent to govern a backwater."

sentences.zh: 」詠劉伶云：「韜精日沈飲，誰知非荒宴。

translations.literal: On Liu Ling he wrote: "Hiding his spirit, he sank daily into drink—who knew it was not reckless feasting?"
translations.idiomatic: Of Liu Ling: "He buried his spirit in daily drinking—who could tell it was not abandon?"

sentences.zh: 」此四句蓋自序也。

translations.literal: These four lines were largely self-description.
translations.idiomatic: Those four lines were largely about himself.

sentences.zh: 湛及義康以其辭旨不遜，大怒，欲黜為遠郡。

translations.literal: Zhan and Yikang, because the tone was insolent, were greatly angered and wished to banish him to a distant commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and Yikang, finding the tone insolent, were furious and meant to exile him to a remote post.

sentences.zh: 文帝與義康詔曰：「宜令思愆里閭，猶復不悛，當驅往東土；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen wrote to Yikang, "Let him reflect on his faults at home; if he still will not reform, drive him to the eastern lands;"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told Yikang, "Have him repent in his neighborhood; if he still will not mend, send him to the eastern provinces;"

sentences.zh: 乃至難恕者，自可隨事錄之。

translations.literal: as for what is truly unpardonable, you may record it as the occasion warrants.
translations.idiomatic: and for what is truly beyond forgiveness, record it as you see fit.

sentences.zh: 」於是延之屏居不豫人間者七載。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanzhi lived in seclusion and took no part in worldly affairs for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi then withdrew from the world for seven years.

sentences.zh: 劉湛誅後，起延之為始興王浚後軍諮議參軍、御史中丞。

translations.literal: After Liu Zhan was executed, Yanzhi was recalled as Rear Army Adviser to Prince Jun of Shixing and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhan's execution he was recalled as rear-army adviser to Prince Jun of Shixing and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 在任從容，無所舉奏。

translations.literal: In office he was at ease and brought no impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: In that post he was easygoing and filed no indictments.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial University and Left Chief of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to director of the Imperial University and left chief clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 何尚之素與延之狎，書與王球曰：「延之有後命，教府無復光暉。

translations.literal: He Shangzhi had long been intimate with Yanzhi and wrote to Wang Qiu, "Yanzhi has a later appointment; the office will no longer shine."
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi, who knew Yanzhi well, wrote Wang Qiu, "Yanzhi has a future appointment—the office will lose its luster."

sentences.zh: 」坐啟買人田不肯還直，尚書左丞荀赤松奏之曰：「求田問舍，前賢所鄙。

translations.literal: For petitioning to buy another man's field and refusing to pay the price, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Chisong memorialized, "Seeking fields and houses is what former worthies despised."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi petitioned to buy a field and refused the price, Left Assistant Director Xun Chisong memorialized: "Seeking fields and houses is what the ancients scorned."

sentences.zh: 延之唯利是視，輕冒陳聞，依傍詔恩，抵捍餘直，垂及周年，猶不畢了。

translations.literal: Yanzhi looks only to profit, lightly dares to petition the throne, relies on imperial grace, resists paying the remainder, and though nearly a year has passed still has not finished.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi eyes profit alone, brazenly appeals to the throne, leans on imperial favor to withhold payment, and after nearly a year still has not settled.

sentences.zh: 昧利苟得，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: He covets gain without regard for anything.
translations.idiomatic: He grasps for gain without scruple.

sentences.zh: 延之昔坐事屏斥，復蒙抽進，而曾不悛革，怨誹無已。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was once dismissed for an offense and again raised by grace, yet he never reformed and his complaints and slanders never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Once banished and then restored, he never mended his ways; complaint and slander never stopped.

sentences.zh: 交遊闒茸，沈迷曲蘖，橫興譏謗，詆毀朝士。

translations.literal: His associates are base; he is sunk in wine, and he raises ridicule and slander, defaming court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps low company, drowns in wine, and spreads mockery, defaming officials at court.

sentences.zh: 仰竊過榮，增憤薄之性，私恃顧眄，成強梁之心。

translations.literal: He secretly enjoys excessive honor and adds to a mean nature; trusting in private favor, he forms a willful heart.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly relishes unmerited rank and feeds a petty temper; counting on private favor, he grows overbearing.

sentences.zh: 外示寡求，內懷奔競，幹祿祈遷，不知極已。

translations.literal: Outwardly he shows little desire, inwardly he races for advancement, scheming for salary and promotion without knowing limit.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he feigns indifference; inwardly he scrambles for office, chasing salary and promotion without end.

sentences.zh: 預宴班觴，肆詈上席。

translations.literal: At banquets in the imperial presence he recklessly reviles those in the upper seats.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts he openly insults those seated above him.

sentences.zh: 山海容含，每存遵養。

translations.literal: Mountains and seas contain all things, yet he is always spared for nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are broad in mercy, yet he is always indulged.

sentences.zh: 愛兼雕蟲，未忍遐棄。

translations.literal: The emperor loves even ornamental talent and cannot bear to cast him far away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cherishes even ornamental talent and will not cast him off.

sentences.zh: 而驕放不節，日月彌甚。

translations.literal: Yet his arrogance grows daily without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his arrogance grows more unrestrained by the day.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聲問過情，孟軻所恥，況聲非外來，問由己出。

translations.literal: I have heard that reputation exceeding reality is what Mencius found shameful—how much more when the noise is not from outside but raised by oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius held it shameful when fame outruns merit—how much worse when the noise is one's own making.

sentences.zh: 雖心智薄劣，而高自比擬，客氣虛張，曾無愧畏。

translations.literal: Though his mind and wisdom are thin and inferior, he compares himself highly; his guest's air is empty and inflated, and he never feels shame or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Though his wit is slight, he sets himself among the great; his manner is all bluster, without shame or fear.

sentences.zh: 豈可復弼亮五教，增耀臺階。

translations.literal: How can he again assist and brighten the Five Teachings and add luster to the terrace steps?
translations.idiomatic: How can he again assist in the Five Teachings and lend luster to the throne?

sentences.zh: 請以延之訟田不實，妄幹天聽，以強陵弱，免所居官。

translations.literal: I ask that Yanzhi, for falsely petitioning over the field and presumptuously reaching the emperor's ear and using strength to bully the weak, be removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yanzhi be removed for false claims over the field, for importuning the throne, and for bullying the weak with his power.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 後為秘書監，光祿勳，太常。

translations.literal: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat, Director of Splendid Honors, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as director of the Secretariat, director of splendid honors, and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時沙門釋慧琳以才學為文帝所賞，朝廷政事多與之謀，遂士庶歸仰。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huilin, valued by Emperor Wen for talent and learning, was often consulted on court affairs, and gentry and commoners alike looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huilin, prized by Emperor Wen for learning, was often consulted on state affairs, and commoners and officials alike looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 上每引見，常升獨榻，延之甚疾焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor received him, he was always given a separate couch; Yanzhi greatly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor received Huilin, the monk sat on a couch apart; Yanzhi resented it deeply.

sentences.zh: 因醉白上曰：「昔同子參乘，袁絲正色。

translations.literal: Drunk, he told the emperor, "In the past Yuan Sili rode with Chao Cuo, and Yuan Sili kept a stern face."
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he told the emperor, "Once Yuan Sili rode with Chao Cuo and kept a stern face."

sentences.zh: 此三台之坐，豈可使刑余居之。

translations.literal: This seat of the Three Terraces—how can it be given to a mutilated man?
translations.idiomatic: How can this seat of the Three Terraces be given to a castrated man?

sentences.zh: 」上變色。

translations.literal: The emperor's face changed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 延之性既褊激，兼有酒過，肆意直言，曾無回隱，故論者多不與之，謂之顏彪。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's nature was narrow and impulsive, and with the fault of wine he spoke freely without concealment; therefore many in discussion would not associate with him, calling him Yan the Tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow and impulsive, and given to wine, he spoke without reserve; many shunned him and called him Tiger Yan.

sentences.zh: 居身儉約，不營財利，布衣蔬食，獨酌郊野。

translations.literal: In his person he was frugal and did not pursue wealth; he wore cloth and ate vegetables and drank alone in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply, pursued no wealth, wore plain cloth, ate vegetables, and drank alone in the outskirts.

sentences.zh: 當其為適，傍若無人。

translations.literal: When he found his ease, it was as if no one were beside him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was at ease, he seemed oblivious to everyone around him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，致事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he retired.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince usurped and enthroned himself, Yanzhi was made Director of Splendid Honors.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince usurped the throne, Yanzhi was made director of splendid honors.

sentences.zh: 長子竣為孝武南中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jun was Adviser to the Southern Army of the Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jun served as adviser to Emperor Xiaowu's southern army.

sentences.zh: 及義師入討，竣定密謀，兼造書檄。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered to punish the usurper, Jun settled the secret plan and also drafted the proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the punitive army marched, Jun shaped the secret plan and drafted the proclamations.

sentences.zh: 劭召延之示以檄文，問曰：「此筆誰造？

translations.literal: Liu Shao summoned Yanzhi and showed him the proclamation, asking, "Whose brush wrote this?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao summoned Yanzhi, showed him the proclamation, and asked, "Whose pen wrote this?"

sentences.zh: 」延之曰：「竣之筆也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi said, "It is Jun's brush."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi said, "Jun's."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「何以知之？

translations.literal: He asked again, "How do you know?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked again, "How do you know?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「竣筆體，臣不容不識。

translations.literal: He said, "Jun's style of writing—your servant cannot fail to recognize it."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I would know Jun's hand anywhere."

sentences.zh: 」劭又曰：「言辭何至乃爾？

translations.literal: Shao also said, "How could the words reach such a point?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao also said, "How could the language go so far?"

sentences.zh: 」延之曰：「竣尚不顧老臣，何能為陛下。

translations.literal: Yanzhi said, "If Jun does not spare an old minister, how could he spare Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi said, "If Jun shows no mercy to an old minister, how would he spare Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」劭意乃釋，由是得免。

translations.literal: Shao's mind was then eased, and by this he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's suspicions eased, and Yanzhi escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 孝武登阼，以為金紫光祿大夫，領湘東王師。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor ascended, Yanzhi was made Director of Splendid Honors with the Gold Seal and concurrently Tutor to Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu took the throne, Yanzhi was made director of splendid honors with the gold seal and tutor to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 嘗與何偃同從上南郊，偃于路中遙呼延之曰：「顏公！

translations.literal: Once, going with He Yan to the southern suburban sacrifice, Yan on the road called from afar, "Master Yan!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying He Yan to the southern suburban rites, Yan called from the road, "Master Yan!"

sentences.zh: 」延之以其輕脫，怪之，答曰：「身非三公之公，又非田舍之公，又非君家阿公，何以見呼為公？

translations.literal: Yanzhi, finding this frivolous, was displeased and replied, "I am neither the 'duke' of the Three Dukes nor the 'duke' of a farmstead, nor your family's uncle—why call me 'duke'?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi, offended by the familiarity, replied, "I am no grand duke, no village elder, nor your uncle—why 'duke'?"

sentences.zh: 」偃羞而退。

translations.literal: Yan withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yan withdrew in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 竣既貴重，權傾一朝，凡所資供，延之一無所受。

translations.literal: Jun had become powerful and his authority tilted the court; whatever supplies were offered, Yanzhi accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had grown powerful and his authority tilted the court, yet Yanzhi accepted none of the provisions sent him.

sentences.zh: 器服不改，宅宇如舊，常乘羸牛車，逢竣鹵簿，即屏住道側。

translations.literal: His vessels and dress were unchanged, his house as before; he often rode a lean ox-cart, and when he met Jun's guard of honor he would step aside from the road.
translations.idiomatic: His dress and furnishings stayed as before; he rode a thin ox-cart, and when he met Jun's escort he pulled aside.

sentences.zh: 又好騎馬遨遊裏巷，遇知舊輒據鞍索酒，得必傾盡，欣然自得。

translations.literal: He also loved to ride through lanes and alleys; meeting old acquaintances he would lean from the saddle and demand wine, and when he got it he would drain the cup and be pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved riding through the lanes; seeing old friends he would lean from the saddle for wine, drain the cup when he got it, and be well pleased.

sentences.zh: 嘗語竣曰：「平生不喜見要人，今不幸見汝。

translations.literal: He once told Jun, "All my life I have disliked meeting important men; now, unhappily, I meet you."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Jun, "All my life I hated meeting the powerful—now, alas, I meet you."

sentences.zh: 」見竣起宅，謂曰：「善為之，無令後人笑汝拙也。

translations.literal: Seeing Jun build a mansion, he said, "Build it well; do not let later men laugh at your clumsiness."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jun build a mansion, he said, "Build it well—don't let posterity laugh at your taste."

sentences.zh: 」表解師職，加給親信二十人。

translations.literal: He memorialized to resign the tutorship and was granted twenty personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to resign the tutorship and was granted twenty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 嘗早候竣，遇賓客盈門，竣方臥不起，延之怒曰：「恭敬撙節，福之基也。

translations.literal: Once he came early to wait on Jun and found guests filling the gate; Jun was still in bed and would not rise. Yanzhi angrily said, "Respect and restraint are the foundation of fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Once he came early to call on Jun and found the gate crowded with guests while Jun lay abed. Yanzhi said angrily, "Respect and restraint are the root of fortune."

sentences.zh: 驕佷傲慢，禍之始也。

translations.literal: Pride and arrogance are the beginning of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Pride and arrogance are the start of ruin.

sentences.zh: 況出糞土之中，而升雲霞之上，傲不可長，其能久乎。」

translations.literal: To rise from the dust to the clouds—pride cannot last; how can it endure long?"
translations.idiomatic: To climb from the dust to the clouds—pride cannot last. How long can it endure?"

sentences.zh: 延之有愛姬，非姬食不飽，寢不安。

translations.literal: Yanzhi had a favorite concubine; without her food he was not sated, without her he could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi kept a favorite concubine; he could neither eat his fill nor sleep without her.

sentences.zh: 姬憑寵，嘗蕩延之墜床致損，竣殺之。

translations.literal: Relying on favor, she once swung on Yanzhi's bed and fell, injuring him; Jun had her killed.
translations.idiomatic: Presuming on favor, she once swung from Yanzhi's bed and fell, hurting him; Jun had her killed.

sentences.zh: 延之痛惜甚至，常坐靈上哭曰：「貴人殺汝，非我殺汝。

translations.literal: Yanzhi grieved beyond measure and often sat before her spirit tablet, weeping, "The noble killed you—it was not I who killed you."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi grieved beyond measure and often wept before her spirit tablet: "The great man killed you—not I."

sentences.zh: 」以冬日臨哭，忽見妾排屏風以壓延之，延之懼墜地，因病。

translations.literal: Weeping at her bier in winter, he suddenly saw the concubine push aside the screen and press on him; Yanzhi feared he would fall and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping at her bier in winter, he suddenly saw the concubine push aside the screen toward him; terrified, he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiaojian 3, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈特進，諡曰憲子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Special Grand Master, with the posthumous title Xianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made special grand master with the posthumous title Xianzi.

sentences.zh: 延之與陳郡謝靈運俱以辭采齊名，而遲速縣絕。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun of Chen Commandery were equally famed for literary brilliance, yet their speed was utterly different.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun of Chen were equally famed for literary brilliance, yet one wrote swiftly and the other slowly.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗各敕擬樂府北上篇，延之受詔便成，靈運久之乃就。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once ordered each to draft a 'Northward' yuefu piece; Yanzhi finished on receiving the command, while Lingyun took long to complete his.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once ordered each to compose a 'Northward' yuefu piece; Yanzhi finished at once, Lingyun only after long labor.

sentences.zh: 延之嘗問鮑照己與靈運優劣，照曰：「謝五言如初發芙蓉，自然可愛。

translations.literal: Yanzhi once asked Bao Zhao whether he or Lingyun was superior; Zhao said, "Xie's five-character verse is like a lotus just opening—naturally lovely."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi once asked Bao Zhao who was better, he or Lingyun. Zhao said, "Xie's pentasyllabic lines are like a lotus just opening—naturally lovely."

sentences.zh: 君詩若鋪錦列繡，亦雕繢滿眼。

translations.literal: Your poems are like brocade spread and embroidery arrayed—also dazzling to the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Your poems are brocade laid out and embroidery hung—dazzling to the eye."

sentences.zh: 」延之每薄湯惠休詩，謂人曰：「惠休製作，委巷中歌謠耳，方當誤後生。

translations.literal: Yanzhi always looked down on Tang Hui Xiu's poems and told people, "Hui Xiu's compositions are alley ballads—they will mislead later generations."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi always scorned Tang Hui Xiu's verse: "Hui Xiu writes alley songs—they will mislead the young."

sentences.zh: 」是時議者以延之、靈運自潘岳、陸機之後，文士莫及，江右稱潘、陸，江左稱顏、謝焉。

translations.literal: Critics of the time held that after Pan Yue and Lu Ji, no literary man matched Yanzhi and Lingyun; south of the Yangzi they spoke of Pan and Lu, east of it of Yan and Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that after Pan Yue and Lu Ji no writer matched Yan and Xie; south of the river they named Pan and Lu, east of it Yan and Xie.

sentences.zh: 竣字士遜，延之長子也。

translations.literal: Jun, courtesy name Shixun, was Yanzhi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Shixun, was Yanzhi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 早有文義，為宋孝武帝撫軍主簿，甚被嘉遇，竣亦盡心補益。

translations.literal: Early he had literary skill and served as Chief Clerk to the Pacification Army of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, greatly favored; Jun also gave his utmost service.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted early in letters, he served as chief clerk to Xiaowu's pacification army and was greatly favored; Jun repaid the trust fully.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，上不欲諸王各立朋黨，將召竣補尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era the emperor did not wish the princes each to form factions and meant to recall Jun to fill a Masters of Writing post.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia the emperor did not want princes forming factions and meant to recall Jun to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 江湛以為在府有稱，不宜回改，乃止。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan held that Jun had reputation in the prince's household and should not be transferred, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan argued that Jun had standing in the prince's household and should not be moved, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉安北、鎮軍、北中郎府主簿。

translations.literal: Following the prince's transfer he served as chief clerk to the Pacification Army, the Army General, and the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince as chief clerk to the pacification army, the army general, and the northern army in turn.

sentences.zh: 初，沙門釋僧含精有學義，謂竣曰：「貧道常見讖記，當有真人應符，名稱次第，屬在殿下。

translations.literal: At first the monk Seng Han, learned and accomplished, told Jun, "This poor monk has often seen prophecies that a true man will answer the omen; by name and order it falls to Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Seng Han, learned and accomplished, told Jun, "I have read prophecies of a true lord to come—the name and order point to Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」後竣在彭城，嘗于親人敘之，言遂宣佈，聞于文帝。

translations.literal: Later Jun, at Pengcheng, spoke of it among kin and the words spread; Emperor Wen heard.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Pengcheng Jun spoke of it among kin; the story spread, and Emperor Wen heard.

sentences.zh: 時元凶巫蠱事已發，故上不加推案。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince's sorcery affair had already broken; therefore the emperor did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's sorcery case had already broken; the emperor did not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮尋陽，遷南中郎記室。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor garrisoned Xunyang, Jun was moved to Recorder of the Southern Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu garrisoned Xunyang, Jun became recorder of the southern army.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，以父延之致仕，固求解職，賜假未發，而文帝崩問至，孝武舉兵入討，轉諮議參軍，領錄事，任總內外，並造檄書。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirtieth year, because his father Yanzhi had retired, he firmly asked to resign; leave was granted but not yet taken when news of Emperor Wen's death arrived; the Filial Emperor raised troops to punish the usurper, and Jun was transferred to Adviser, concurrently handling records and drafting proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the thirtieth year, with Yanzhi retired, he asked to resign; leave was granted but not yet taken when word came of Wen's death. Xiaowu raised arms to punish the usurper; Jun became adviser, handled records, and drafted proclamations.

sentences.zh: 孝武發尋陽，便有疾，自沈慶之以下並不堪相見，唯竣出入臥內，斷決軍機。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor set out from Xunyang he fell ill; from Shen Qingzhi down none could bear to see him—only Jun went in and out of the sickroom and decided military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu fell ill leaving Xunyang; from Shen Qingzhi down none could face him—only Jun entered the sickroom and decided military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時孝武屢經危篤，不任諮稟，凡厥眾務，竣皆專斷施行。

translations.literal: The Filial Emperor repeatedly hovered near death and could not attend to counsel; all other affairs Jun decided and executed on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu repeatedly hovered near death and could not govern; Jun decided and executed all other affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 南郡王義宣、臧質等反，以竣兼領右將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Nanjun Yixuan and Zang Zhi and others rebelled, Jun was concurrently given command as General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixuan of Nanjun and Zang Zhi rebelled, Jun was concurrently made general of the right.

sentences.zh: 義宣、質諸子藏匿建康、秣陵、湖熟、江寧縣界，孝武大怒，免丹陽尹褚湛之官，收四縣官長，以竣為丹陽尹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The sons of Yixuan, Zhi, and others were hidden within the boundaries of Jiankang, Moling, Hushu, and Jiangning; the Filial Emperor was greatly angered, removed Administrator of Danyang Chu Zhanzhi, arrested the magistrates of the four counties, and made Jun Administrator of Danyang, with concurrent title as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' sons were hidden in Jiankang, Moling, Hushu, and Jiangning; Xiaowu was furious, removed Danyang administrator Chu Zhanzhi, arrested the four county magistrates, and made Jun Danyang administrator with concurrent rank as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 先是，竣未有子，而大司馬江夏王義恭諸子為元凶所殺，至是各產男，上自為制名，名義恭子為伯禽，以比魯公伯禽，周公之子。

translations.literal: Earlier Jun had no sons; the sons of Grand Marshal Prince Yixong of Jiangxia had been killed by the usurper. Now each bore a son; the emperor himself chose names—Yixong's son was called Boqin, likened to Boqin, son of the Duke of Lu, son of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had no sons yet; Prince Yixong of Jiangxia's sons had been killed by the usurper. Now each house had a boy; the emperor named them himself—Yixong's son Boqin, likened to the Duke of Lu's Boqin, son of the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 名竣子為辟強，以比漢侍中辟強，張良之子也。

translations.literal: Jun's son was named Biqiang, likened to Biqiang, attendant at the court of Han, son of Zhang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son was named Biqiang, likened to Biqiang the Han attendant, Zhang Liang's son.

sentences.zh: 先是，元嘉中鑄四銖錢，輪郭形制與五銖同，用費損無利，故百姓不盜鑄。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Yuanjia, four-zhu coins were cast; rim and form matched the five-zhu, and because cost exceeded profit the people did not illicitly cast.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia four-zhu coins had been cast with rims like the five-zhu; costs exceeded profit, so people did not counterfeit.

sentences.zh: 及孝武即位，又鑄孝建四銖，所鑄錢形式薄小，輪郭不成，於是人間盜鑄者雜以鉛錫，並不牢固。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor ascended, Xiaojian four-zhu were cast again; the coins were thin and small, the rims incomplete, and then among the people illicit casters mixed in lead and tin, and none were solid.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu took the throne Xiaojian four-zhu were cast again—thin, small, with incomplete rims; counterfeiters mixed in lead and tin, and the coins would not hold.

sentences.zh: 又翦鑿古錢以取其銅，錢轉薄小，稍違官式。

translations.literal: They also clipped and chiseled old coins to take the copper; the coins grew thinner and smaller and gradually departed from the official standard.
translations.idiomatic: People clipped old coins for copper; the money grew thinner and drifted from the standard.

sentences.zh: 雖重制嚴刑，人吏官長坐死免者相系，而盜鑄彌甚，百物踴貴，人患苦之。

translations.literal: Though severe punishments were reimposed, officials and magistrates were executed or removed in succession, yet illicit casting grew worse, prices soared, and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Though punishments grew harsher and officials fell in succession, counterfeiting worsened, prices soared, and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 乃立品格，薄小無輪郭者悉加禁斷。

translations.literal: Grades of coin were then established; thin small coins without rims were all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Coin grades were set; thin rimless coins were banned.

sentences.zh: 始興公沈慶之議：「宜聽人鑄錢。

translations.literal: Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi proposed: "It should be permitted for people to cast coin."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, proposed: "Private casting should be allowed."

sentences.zh: 置署，樂鑄之家皆居署內。

translations.literal: Offices should be set up; families pleased to cast should all dwell within the offices.
translations.idiomatic: Offices should be set up; willing casters should live within them.

sentences.zh: 去春所禁新品，一時施用，今鑄悉依此格。

translations.literal: The new coins forbidden last spring should be used for the time being; all casting now should follow this standard.
translations.idiomatic: Last spring's banned new coins should be used for now; all new casting should follow that standard.

sentences.zh: 萬稅三千，嚴檢盜鑄，並禁翦鑿。

translations.literal: Ten thousand coins taxed three thousand; illicit casting strictly inspected, and clipping also forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Tax three thousand per ten thousand coins; strictly inspect counterfeiting and forbid clipping.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，公私豐贍，銅盡事息，奸偽自止。

translations.literal: Within a few years public and private would be rich, copper would be exhausted and the affair would cease, and fraud would stop of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years treasury and people would prosper, copper would run out and fraud would cease.

sentences.zh: 禁鑄則銅轉成器，開鑄則器化為財。

translations.literal: Forbid casting and copper becomes vessels; open casting and vessels become wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Ban casting and copper becomes vessels; allow casting and vessels become coin.

sentences.zh: 」上下其事於公卿，竣議曰：「今雲開署放鑄，誠所欲同，但慮采山事絕，器用日耗。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the high ministers; Jun argued, "Now you say open offices and allow casting—indeed this is what I too wish, but I fear mining will cease and daily use will be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the high ministers. Jun argued: "Opening offices for casting is what I too would wish—but mining may cease and daily use be exhausted."

sentences.zh: 銅既轉少，器亦彌貴。

translations.literal: As copper grows less, vessels also grow costlier.
translations.idiomatic: As copper grows scarce, vessels grow costlier.

sentences.zh: 設器直一千，則鑄之減半，為之無利，雖令不行。

translations.literal: Suppose a vessel worth a thousand—casting would halve it and yield no profit; though ordered, it would not be done.
translations.idiomatic: If a vessel worth a thousand yields only half that in coin, there is no profit; the order would fail.

sentences.zh: 」時議者又以銅難得，欲鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: Discussants also held copper hard to obtain and wished to cast two-zhu coins.
translations.idiomatic: Others held copper scarce and wished to cast two-zhu coins.

sentences.zh: 竣又議曰：「今鑄二銖，恣行新細，于官無解於乏，而人奸巧大興，天下之貨將糜碎至盡。

translations.literal: Jun again argued, "If two-zhu are cast now and the new thin coins run freely, the state gains nothing in shortage while human cunning rises greatly—the realm's currency will be ground to fragments."
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued again: "Cast two-zhu now and let thin new coins circulate freely—the state gains nothing while fraud flourishes and the realm's currency is ground to dust."

sentences.zh: 空曰嚴禁，而利深難絕，不過一二年間，其弊不可復救。

translations.literal: Empty talk of strict prohibition while profit runs deep and is hard to cut off—in no more than a year or two the harm cannot be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Strict bans mean nothing when profit runs deep—in a year or two the harm will be beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 此其甚不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first great impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first great objection.

sentences.zh: 使奸人意騁，而貽厥愆謀，此又甚不可二也。

translations.literal: Letting cunning men run free and bequeathing guilt to posterity—this is the second great impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Letting the cunning run free and bequeathing guilt to posterity is the second.

sentences.zh: 富商得志，貧人因窘，此又甚不可三也。

translations.literal: Rich merchants have their way while the poor are pressed—this is the third great impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants prosper while the poor are squeezed—that is the third.

sentences.zh: 若使交益深重，尚不可行，況又未見利，而眾弊如此，失算當時，取笑百代乎。

translations.literal: If trade grew heavier it would still be unworkable—how much less when no benefit is seen and the many harms are as they are; to miscount at the time is to be laughed at for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Even deep trade would be unworkable; with no benefit seen and harms so plain, to choose this now is to be mocked for generations.

sentences.zh: 」前廢帝即位，鑄二銖，形式轉細，官錢每出，人間即模效之，而大小厚薄皆不及也。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, two-zhu were cast; the form grew still thinner, and whenever official coin went out the people at once copied it, yet size and thickness never matched.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne two-zhu were cast, thinner still; whenever official coin appeared the people copied it, never matching size or thickness.

sentences.zh: 無輪郭，不磨鑢，如今之翦鑿者，謂之耒子錢。

translations.literal: Without rims, unfiled, like today's clipped coins—they were called 'plowshare coins.'
translations.idiomatic: Rimless, unfiled, like today's clipped coins—they were called plowshare coins.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，沈慶之啟通私鑄，由是錢貨亂敗，一千錢長不盈三寸，大小稱此，謂之鵝眼錢；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe, Shen Qingzhi memorialized to allow private casting; thereby currency was thrown into chaos—a thousand coins strung did not fill three inches; coins of this size were called 'goose-eye coins';
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe 1 Shen Qingzhi urged private casting; currency collapsed—a thousand coins strung did not fill three inches; such were called goose-eye coins;

sentences.zh: 劣於此者謂之綖環錢。

translations.literal: worse than these were called 'thread-ring coins.'
translations.idiomatic: worse still were thread-ring coins.

sentences.zh: 貫之以縷，入水不沈，隨手破碎，市井不復料數，十萬錢不盈一掬。

translations.literal: Strung on thread they would not sink in water and broke at a touch; the market no longer counted them—a hundred thousand coins did not fill one handful.
translations.idiomatic: Strung on thread they floated and broke at a touch; markets no longer counted them— a hundred thousand did not fill one handful.

sentences.zh: 斗米一萬，商貨不行。

translations.literal: A dou of rice cost ten thousand; commerce ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A dou of rice cost ten thousand; trade stopped.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，唯禁鵝眼、綖環，其餘皆通用。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign only goose-eye and thread-ring coins were forbidden; the rest remained in use.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ming's reign only goose-eye and thread-ring coins were banned; the rest circulated.

sentences.zh: 復禁人鑄，官署亦廢，尋復普斷，唯用古錢。

translations.literal: Private casting was forbidden again and government offices also abolished; soon a general ban returned and only old coins were used.
translations.idiomatic: Private casting was banned again and government mints abolished; soon all new coin was banned and only old money used.

sentences.zh: 竣自散騎常侍、丹陽尹加中書令，表讓中書令，見許。

translations.literal: Jun, from Regular Attendant and Administrator of Danyang, was promoted to Director of the Secretariat; he memorialized to decline the directorship and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun rose from regular attendant and Danyang administrator to director of the Secretariat; he declined the directorship and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 時歲旱人饑，竣上言禁餳一月，息米近萬斛。

translations.literal: In a year of drought and famine Jun memorialized to forbid malt sugar for one month, saving nearly ten thousand hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: In drought and famine he memorialized to forbid malt sugar for one month, saving nearly ten thousand hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 復代謝莊為吏部尚書，領太子右衛率，未拜，丁父憂。

translations.literal: He replaced Xie Zhuang as Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, but before taking office he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Xie Zhuang as director of the Masters of Writing and right commandant of the heir's guard, but before taking office mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 裁踰月，起為右將軍，丹陽尹如故。

translations.literal: Barely a month later he was recalled as General of the Right, still Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later he was recalled as general of the right, still Danyang administrator.

sentences.zh: 竣固辭，表十上不許。

translations.literal: Jun firmly declined; ten memorials were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun declined firmly; ten memorials went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人戴明寶抱竣登車，載之郡舍。

translations.literal: An Attendant of the Secretariat, Dai Mingbao, was sent to lift Jun into the carriage and convey him to the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Dai Mingbao was sent to lift Jun into the carriage and take him to the yamen.

sentences.zh: 賜以布衣一襲，絮以彩綸，遣主衣就衣諸體。

translations.literal: He was granted one suit of plain cloth padded with colored silk, and a master of robes was sent to dress his whole body.
translations.idiomatic: He was given plain cloth padded with colored silk and a master of robes to dress him.

sentences.zh: 及王僧達被誅，謂為所讒構，臨死陳竣前後忿懟，恨言不見從。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengda was executed, Jun believed himself slandered; on the verge of death Sengda stated Jun's earlier rancor and regret that his words were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengda was executed, Jun believed himself slandered; dying, Sengda cited Jun's old rancor and regret that his warnings went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 僧達所言，頗相符會，上乃使御史中丞庾徽之奏竣：「窺覘國柄，潛圖久執。

translations.literal: What Sengda said largely matched; the emperor then had Censor-in-Chief Yu Huizhi memorialize against Jun: "He spies on the handle of state and secretly plots long tenure."
translations.idiomatic: Sengda's words largely matched; the emperor had Censor-in-Chief Yu Huizhi indict Jun: "He spies on the handle of state and plots long tenure."

sentences.zh: 受任選曹，驅扇滋甚，出尹京輦，形勢彌放。

translations.literal: Receiving charge of the Selection Bureau he fanned faction more fiercely; sent out as capital intendant his power grew bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Given the Selection Bureau he fanned faction; as capital intendant his power grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 傳詔犯憲，舊須啟聞，而竣以通訴忤己，輒加鞭辱，罔顧威靈，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Transmitting edicts in violation of law formerly required reporting; Jun, because the messenger's appeal offended him, had him whipped and shamed—disregard for authority could go no further.
translations.idiomatic: Transmitting edicts against law once required report; Jun had a messenger whipped for appealing to him—none showed such contempt for authority.

sentences.zh: 懷挾奸數，包藏隱慝，豫聞中旨，罔不宣露。

translations.literal: He harbored treacherous schemes and concealed guilt; hearing the emperor's inmost intent he always disclosed it.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored treachery; hearing the emperor's inmost intent he always disclosed it.

sentences.zh: 罰則委上，善必歸己，脅懼上宰，激動閭閻。

translations.literal: Punishment he ascribed upward, merit he kept for himself; he intimidated the chief minister and stirred the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: He ascribed punishment upward and kept merit for himself; he intimidated the chief minister and stirred the lanes.

sentences.zh: 末慮上聞，內懷猜懼，偽請東牧，以卜天旨。

translations.literal: Fearing the emperor would hear, inwardly he was suspicious and falsely asked for an eastern post to test heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor would hear, he falsely asked for an eastern post to test heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 既獲出藩，怨詈方肆，反唇腹誹，方之已輕。

translations.literal: Once he gained a frontier post he cursed freely; turning his lips in secret slander, even that was mild.
translations.idiomatic: Once sent to the frontier he cursed freely; secret slander was the least of it.

sentences.zh: 前冬母亡，詔賜還葬，事畢不去，盤桓經時。

translations.literal: Last winter his mother died; an edict granted return for burial, yet when the rites were done he did not leave and lingered for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter his mother died; he was granted return for burial but lingered long after the rites.

sentences.zh: 方構間勳貴，造立同異，遂以己被斥外，國道將顛。

translations.literal: He was then sowing division among meritorious nobles and creating factions, saying that because he himself was cast out the state's way would topple.
translations.idiomatic: He sowed division among meritorious nobles, claiming that because he was cast out the state would fall.

sentences.zh: 兼行闕於家，早負世議，天倫怨毒，親交震駭。

translations.literal: His conduct at home was lacking and he had long borne public censure; kinship turned to poison and friends were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct at home was lacking and public censure long; kinship turned poisonous and friends were shaken.

sentences.zh: 街談道說，非復風聲，宜加顯戮，以昭盛化。

translations.literal: Street talk was no longer mere rumor; he should receive conspicuous punishment to display the great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Street talk was no longer rumor; he should be punished openly to display reform.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免竣所居官，下太常削爵土。

translations.literal: I ask that for the present matter Jun be removed from office and the Minister of Ceremonies be ordered to strip rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Jun be removed and the Minister of Ceremonies strip rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 」上未欲便加大戮，且止免官。

translations.literal: The emperor did not yet wish to impose death and only stopped at removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not yet wish to kill him and only removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 竣頻啟謝罪，並乞性命。

translations.literal: Jun repeatedly memorialized to apologize and also begged for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Jun repeatedly apologized and begged for his life.

sentences.zh: 上愈怒，詔答曰：「憲司所奏，非宿昔所以相期。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier and replied by edict, "What the censor memorializes is not what we long expected from each other."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier: "What the censor reports is not what we once expected of each other."

sentences.zh: 卿受榮遇，政當極此。

translations.literal: You received glory and favor and should have reached this limit.
translations.idiomatic: You received glory and favor and should have reached this limit.

sentences.zh: 訕訐怨憤，已孤本望，乃復過煩思慮，懼不全立，豈為下事上誠節之至邪。」

translations.literal: Slander, complaint, and resentment have already betrayed my original hope; now you again trouble me with anxious thoughts, fearing you cannot stand whole—is this the utmost sincerity of a subject serving his lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Slander and resentment have already betrayed my hope; now you trouble me with anxious pleas—is this the sincerity of a subject?"

sentences.zh: 及竟陵王誕為逆，因此陷之，言通於誕。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling Dan rebelled, by this Jun was implicated, said to have communicated with Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Jun was implicated as having communicated with him.

sentences.zh: 召御史中丞庾徽之於前立奏，奏成，詔先打折足，然後於獄賜死，妻息宥之以遠。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Yu Huizhi was summoned before the emperor to draft the memorial; when it was done, an edict first ordered his legs broken, then execution in prison; wife and children were spared and sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huizhi was summoned to draft the indictment; when done, an edict ordered his legs broken, then death in prison; wife and children were spared and sent away.

sentences.zh: 子辟強徙交州，又于宮亭湖沈殺之。

translations.literal: His son Biqiang was exiled to Jiaozhou and then drowned in Lake Gongting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biqiang was exiled to Jiaozhou and drowned in Lake Gongting.

sentences.zh: 竣文集行於世。

translations.literal: Jun's collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's collected writings circulated.

sentences.zh: 竣弟測亦以文章見知，官至江夏王義恭大司馬錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Ce was also known for writing and reached Recorder of the Grand Marshal under Prince Yixong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother Ce was also known for writing and reached recorder under Prince Yixong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 以兄貴為憂，先竣卒。

translations.literal: He grieved that his brother's rank brought trouble and died before Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved that his brother's rank brought trouble and died before Jun.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，詔曰：「延之昔師訓朕躬，情契兼重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, an edict said, "Yanzhi once tutored my person with affection and weight together."
translations.idiomatic: When Ming ascended, an edict said, "Yanzhi once tutored me with deep affection."

sentences.zh: 前記室參軍、濟陽太守啜，伏事蕃朝，綢繆恩舊，可擢為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Former Recorder Huan, Administrator of Jiyang, served the princely court faithfully and may be promoted to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Former recorder Huan, administrator of Jiyang, served the princely court faithfully and may be promoted to secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 」奐，延之第三子也。

translations.literal: Huan was Yanzhi's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was Yanzhi's third son.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯字長深，竣族兄也。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo, courtesy name Changshen, was Jun's clansman elder.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo, styled Changshen, was Jun's elder clansman.

sentences.zh: 父邵，剛正有局力，為謝晦領軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Shao was upright and forceful and served as Chief of Staff to Xie Hui, General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao was upright and forceful and served as chief of staff to Xie Hui, general of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 晦鎮江陵，請為諮議參軍，領錄事，軍府之務悉委焉。

translations.literal: When Hui garrisoned Jiangling he requested Shibo as Adviser, concurrently handling records; all military affairs of the headquarters were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui garrisoned Jiangling he made Shibo adviser and recorder; all headquarters affairs were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 邵慮晦有禍，求為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Shao feared Hui would meet disaster and asked to be Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Shao feared disaster for Hui and asked to be administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 未及之郡，會晦見討，邵飲藥死。

translations.literal: Before reaching the commandery, Hui was punished; Shao drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching his post, Hui was punished; Shao took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 師伯少孤貧，涉獵書傳，頗解聲樂。

translations.literal: Shibo was orphaned young and poor; he ranged through books and was fairly skilled in music.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo was orphaned and poor; he read widely and knew music fairly well.

sentences.zh: 弟師仲妻，臧質女也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shizhong's wife was the daughter of Zang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shizhong's wife was Zang Zhi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 質為徐州，辟師伯為主簿。

translations.literal: Zhi was in Xuzhou and recruited Shibo as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, in Xuzhou, recruited Shibo as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孝武為徐州，師伯仍為輔國安北行參軍。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor was in Xuzhou, Shibo still served as Aide to the Pacification Army of the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu was in Xuzhou, Shibo still served as aide to the northern pacification army.

sentences.zh: 王景文時為諮議參軍，愛其諧敏，進之孝武，以為徐州主簿。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwen was then Adviser and, loving his quick wit, recommended him to the Filial Emperor, who made him Chief Clerk of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen, then an adviser, admired his quick wit and recommended him to Xiaowu, who made him chief clerk of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 善於附會，大被知遇。

translations.literal: Skilled at ingratiating himself, he was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at ingratiating himself, he won great favor.

sentences.zh: 及去鎮，師伯以主簿送故。

translations.literal: When the prince left his garrison Shibo escorted him as chief clerk on the farewell journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince left his post Shibo escorted him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮尋陽，啟文帝請為南中郎府主簿，文帝不許，謂典簽曰：「中郎府主簿，那得用顏師伯。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor garrisoned Xunyang he memorialized Emperor Wen to make Shibo chief clerk of the Southern Army; Wen refused and told the registrar, "The Southern Army chief clerk—how can Yan Shibo be used?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu garrisoned Xunyang he asked Wen to make Shibo southern-army chief clerk; Wen refused: "How can Shibo hold that post?"

sentences.zh: 」孝武啟為長流正佐，帝又曰：「朝廷不能除之，郎可自板，然亦不宜署長流。

translations.literal: The Filial Emperor memorialized to make him Senior Clerk of the Long Stream, chief assistant; the emperor again said, "The court cannot remove him; you may appoint him yourself by plaque, yet he should not hold the long-stream post either."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu asked for him as senior clerk of the long stream; Wen said, "The court cannot remove him—you may appoint by plaque, but not to long stream."

sentences.zh: 」乃板為參軍刑獄。

translations.literal: He was then appointed by plaque as Adviser for Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed by plaque as adviser for punishments.

sentences.zh: 及討元凶，轉主簿。

translations.literal: When the usurper was punished he was transferred to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper was punished he became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孝武踐阼，以為黃門侍郎，累遷侍中。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor ascended he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and repeatedly promoted to Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu took the throne he became attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and rose to attendant.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，封平都縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu District.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 1 he was enfeoffed as marquis of Pingdu district.

sentences.zh: 親幸隆密，群臣莫二。

translations.literal: Favored intimately and closely—among the ministers none was second.
translations.idiomatic: Favored intimately—among ministers none was second.

sentences.zh: 多納貨賄，家累千金。

translations.literal: He accepted many bribes and his household accumulated a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: He took many bribes and his household amassed a thousand gold.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘗與師伯摴蒱，帝擲得雉，大悅，謂必勝。

translations.literal: The Filial Emperor once played bo with Shibo; the emperor threw the pheasant and was greatly pleased, thinking he must win.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu once played bo with Shibo; the emperor threw the pheasant and was pleased, sure of victory.

sentences.zh: 師伯後得盧，帝失色，師伯遽斂子曰：「幾作盧。

translations.literal: Shibo later got the deer; the emperor's face fell; Shibo quickly gathered the dice and said, "Nearly made the deer."
translations.idiomatic: Shibo later threw the deer; the emperor's face fell; Shibo quickly gathered the dice: "Nearly the deer."

sentences.zh: 」爾日，師伯一輸百萬。

translations.literal: That day Shibo lost a million in one throw.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shibo lost a million in one throw.

sentences.zh: 仍遷吏部尚書、右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made director of the Masters of Writing and general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 上不欲威權在下，前後領選者唯奉行文書，師伯專情獨斷，奏無不可。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish authority to rest below; former directors of selection only carried out documents—Shibo decided alone and no memorial was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not want power below; past selection chiefs only carried papers—Shibo decided alone and nothing was refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時分置二選，陳郡謝莊、琅邪王曇生並為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At that time selection was divided in two; Xie Zhuang of Chen and Wang Tansheng of Langye were both Directors of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Selection was then split; Xie Zhuang of Chen and Wang Tansheng of Langye were both directors.

sentences.zh: 師伯子舉周旋寒人張奇為公車令，上以奇資品不當，使兼市買丞，以蔡道惠代之。

translations.literal: Shibo's son promoted the low-born Zhang Qi to Director of the Public Carriages; the emperor held Qi's qualification unfit and had him concurrently Market-buying Assistant; Cai Daohui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo's son promoted the low-born Zhang Qi to director of the public carriages; the emperor held Qi unfit and made him market-buying assistant; Cai Daohui replaced him.

sentences.zh: 令史潘道棲、褚道惠、顏禕之、元從夫、任澹之、石道兒、黃難、周公選等抑道惠敕，使奇先到公車，不施行奇兼市買丞事。

translations.literal: Clerks Pan Daoqi, Chu Daohui, Yan Yizhi, Yuan Congfu, Ren Tanzhi, Shi Dao'er, Huang Nan, Zhou Gongxuan and others suppressed Daohui's order and made Qi reach the public carriages first, not carrying out Qi's concurrent market-buying duty.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks Pan Daoqi and others suppressed Daohui's order so Qi reached the public carriages first without taking the market-buying post.

sentences.zh: 師伯坐以子預職，莊、曇生免官，道棲、道惠棄市，禕之等六人鞭杖一百。

translations.literal: Shibo was punished because his son foreknew the office; Zhuang and Tansheng were removed; Daoqi and Daohui were executed in the market; Yizhi and the other six were flogged a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo was punished because his son foreknew the post; Zhuang and Tansheng were removed; Daoqi and Daohui were executed; six others were flogged.

sentences.zh: 師伯尋領太子中庶人，雖被黜挫，受任如初。

translations.literal: Shibo soon took concurrent post as Attendant of the Heir Apparent; though demoted, he was entrusted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo soon became attendant to the heir apparent; though demoted, he was trusted as before.

sentences.zh: 師伯居權日久，天下輻協，遊其門者，爵位莫不踰分。

translations.literal: Shibo had long held power; the realm converged on him—those who visited his gate received rank beyond their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Long in power, he drew the realm to his gate; visitors won rank beyond their measure.

sentences.zh: 多納貨賄，家產豐積，妓妾聲樂，盡天下之選，園池第宅，冠絕當時，驕奢淫恣，為衣冠所疾。

translations.literal: He accepted many bribes; his estate was rich; singing girls and music were chosen from all under heaven; gardens, pools, mansions, and houses surpassed the age; proud, extravagant, and dissolute—gentry and officials resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes; his estate was vast; singers and gardens surpassed the age; proud and dissolute—officials resented him.

sentences.zh: 又遷尚書僕射，領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made vice director of the Masters of Writing and Danyang administrator.

sentences.zh: 廢帝欲親朝政，轉師伯為左僕射。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor wished to attend to court himself and transferred Shibo to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor wished to govern himself and moved Shibo to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書王景文為右僕射。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwen, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen, director of the Masters of Writing, became right vice director.

sentences.zh: 奪其京尹，又分台任。

translations.literal: His capital intendant post was taken and the platform duties divided.
translations.idiomatic: His capital post was taken and platform duties divided.

sentences.zh: 師伯至是始懼，與柳元景謀廢立。

translations.literal: Shibo then began to fear and plotted with Liu Yuanjing to depose and enthrone.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo then feared and plotted with Liu Yuanjing to depose the emperor.

sentences.zh: 初，師伯專斷朝事，不與沈慶之參懷，謂令史曰：「沈公爪牙者耳，安得預政事。

translations.literal: At first Shibo monopolized court affairs and did not consult Shen Qingzhi; he told a clerk, "Lord Shen is only a claw and fang—how can he share in government?"
translations.idiomatic: At first Shibo monopolized court affairs without consulting Shen Qingzhi: "Shen is only claws and fangs—how can he share government?"

sentences.zh: 」慶之聞而切齒，乃泄其謀。

translations.literal: Qingzhi heard and gnashed his teeth, then leaked the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi heard, gnashed his teeth, and leaked the plot.

sentences.zh: 尋與太宰江夏王義恭同誅，六子皆見殺。

translations.literal: Soon he was executed together with Grand Tutor Prince Yixong of Jiangxia; six sons were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was executed with Grand Tutor Prince Yixong of Jiangxia; six sons were killed.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，諡曰荒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, the posthumous title was Huang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming ascended, his posthumous title was Huang.

sentences.zh: 沈懷文

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen

sentences.zh: 沈懷文字思明，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiwen, courtesy name Siming, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen, styled Siming, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖寂，晉光祿勳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji served as Director of Splendid Honors in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji was director of splendid honors under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父宣，新安太守。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 懷文少好玄理，善為文章，為楚昭王二妃詩，見稱於世。

translations.literal: Huaiwen in youth loved arcane principle and was skilled at writing; his poem on the two consorts of King Zhao of Chu was praised in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen loved arcane learning in youth and wrote well; his poem on King Zhao of Chu's two consorts was praised.

sentences.zh: 為江夏王義恭東合祭酒。

translations.literal: He served as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under Prince Yixong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He served as eastern-pavilion libationer under Prince Yixong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，新安郡送故豐厚，奉終禮畢，余悉班之親戚，一無所留。

translations.literal: In mourning for his father the Xin'an commandery sent a lavish farewell; when the rites were finished he distributed the remainder among kin and kept nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his father, Xin'an sent lavish funeral gifts; when rites ended he gave all to kin and kept nothing.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而嘉之，賜奴婢六人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and commended him, granting six male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen commended him and granted six servants.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became gentleman of the palace section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 隱士雷次宗被征居鍾山，後南還廬江。

translations.literal: The recluse Lei Cizong was summoned to dwell on Mount Zhong and later returned south to Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Lei Cizong, summoned to Mount Zhong, later returned south to Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 何尚之設祖道，文義之士畢集。

translations.literal: He Shangzhi set a farewell feast; men of letters all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi gave a farewell feast; men of letters gathered.

sentences.zh: 為連句詩，懷文所作尤美，辭高一座。

translations.literal: They composed linked-verse poetry; what Huaiwen wrote was especially fine and topped the company in language.
translations.idiomatic: They composed linked verse; Huaiwen's lines were finest and topped the company.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕鎮襄陽，出為後軍主簿，與諮議參軍謝莊共掌辭令，領義成太守。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan garrisoned Xiangyang he went out as Chief Clerk of the Rear Army, shared charge of documents with Adviser Xie Zhuang, and concurrently served as Administrator of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan garrisoned Xiangyang he became rear-army chief clerk, shared documents with Xie Zhuang, and governed Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，誕當為廣州，欲以懷文為安南府記室，先除通直郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, when Dan was to go to Guangzhou he wished to make Huaiwen Recorder of the Pacification Army and first appointed him Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 28, when Dan was to go to Guangzhou he wished Huaiwen as pacification-army recorder and first made him direct attendant.

sentences.zh: 懷文固辭南行，上不悅。

translations.literal: Huaiwen firmly declined the southern journey; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen declined the southern journey; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 弟懷遠納東陽公主養女王鸚鵡為妾，元凶行巫蠱，鸚鵡豫之，事泄，懷文因此失調，為治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huaiyuan took the Princess of Dongyang's foster daughter Wang Yingwu as concubine; the usurper practiced sorcery and Yingwu took part; when the affair leaked Huaiwen lost favor and was made Drafting Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Huaiyuan took Princess Dongyang's foster daughter Yingwu as concubine; the usurper's sorcery case implicated her; Huaiwen lost favor and became drafting censor.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the usurper seized the throne he was made Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper seized the throne he was made secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 孝武入討，呼之使作符檄，固辭。

translations.literal: When the Filial Emperor entered to punish the usurper he was summoned to write talismans and proclamations and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu marched to punish the usurper he was summoned to write proclamations and declined.

sentences.zh: 劭大怒，會殷沖救得免。

translations.literal: Shao was greatly angered; Yin Chong's rescue allowed escape.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was furious; Yin Chong's intervention saved him.

sentences.zh: 托疾落馬，間行奔新亭，以為竟陵王誕驃騎錄事參軍、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: Feigning illness he fell from a horse, went secretly to Xinting, and was made Recorder under Prince Dan of Jingling and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: Feigning illness he fell from a horse, fled secretly to Xinting, and served Prince Dan of Jingling as recorder and Huailing administrator.

sentences.zh: 時國哀未釋，誕欲起內齋。

translations.literal: At that time national mourning was not yet lifted; Dan wished to hold an inner fast.
translations.idiomatic: National mourning was not yet lifted; Dan wished to hold an inner fast.

sentences.zh: 懷文以為不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Huaiwen held it impossible and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said it was wrong and Dan stopped.

sentences.zh: 尋轉揚州中從事史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Central Army Aide of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became central-army aide of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 時議省錄尚書，懷文以為非宜，上議不從。

translations.literal: At that time some proposed abolishing the recording Masters of Writing; Huaiwen held it unfitting and the upper discussion did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed abolishing the recording Masters of Writing; Huaiwen held it unfitting and the court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 遷別駕從事史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Aide and Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to aide and attendant.

sentences.zh: 及江夏王義恭遷西陽王子尚為揚州，居職如故。

translations.literal: When Prince Yixong of Jiangxia was moved and Prince Zishang of Xiyang became Inspector of Yangzhou, Huaiwen's duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixong was moved and Prince Zishang of Xiyang became Yangzhou inspector, Huaiwen's duties stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 時熒惑守南斗，上乃廢西州舊館，使子尚移居東城以厭之。

translations.literal: When the Fire Star guarded the Southern Dipper the emperor abolished the old Western Province residence and had Zishang move to the eastern city to appease it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fire Star guarded the Southern Dipper the emperor abolished the old Western Province residence and moved Zishang to the eastern city to appease it.

sentences.zh: 懷文曰：「天道示變，宜應之以德，今雖空西州，恐無益也。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "Heaven shows change; one should answer with virtue. Now though the Western Province is emptied, I fear it will not help."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "Heaven shows change; answer with virtue. Emptying the Western Province may not help."

sentences.zh: 」不從，而西州竟廢。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow, and the Western Province was indeed abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen, and the Western Province was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，遷尚書吏部郎，時朝議欲依古制置立王畿，揚州移居會稽，猶以星變故也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was promoted to Director of Personnel of the Masters of Writing; at that time court discussion wished to follow antiquity and establish a royal domain, moving Yangzhou to Kuaiji—again because of the stellar omen.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 2 he became director of personnel; court then debated establishing a royal domain and moving Yangzhou to Kuaiji—again because of the omen.

sentences.zh: 懷文曰：「周制封畿，漢置司隸，各因時宜，非存相反。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "The Zhou system enfeoffed the domain; Han set the Metropolitan Commandant—each suited its time, not inherently opposed."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "Zhou enfeoffed the domain; Han set the metropolitan commandant—each suited its time, not opposed in essence."

sentences.zh: 安人定國，其揆一也。

translations.literal: To settle people and stabilize the state—the measure is one.
translations.idiomatic: Settling people and stabilizing the state follow one measure.

sentences.zh: 苟人心所安，天亦從之。

translations.literal: If the people's hearts are at ease, heaven too will follow.
translations.idiomatic: If hearts are at ease, heaven follows.

sentences.zh: 未必改今追古，乃致平一。

translations.literal: It is not certain that changing the present to pursue antiquity will bring unity.
translations.idiomatic: Changing the present to chase antiquity will not necessarily bring unity.

sentences.zh: 神州舊壤，歷代相承，異于邊州，或置或罷。

translations.literal: The old lands of the divine province have been handed down through generations, unlike frontier provinces now set up or now abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The old lands of the divine province have passed through generations, unlike frontier provinces set up or abolished at will.

sentences.zh: 既物情不悅，容虧化本。

translations.literal: Since sentiment is displeased, it may damage the root of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Since hearts are displeased, the root of good governance may be harmed.

sentences.zh: 」又不從。

translations.literal: Again the emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 三年，子尚移鎮會稽。

translations.literal: In the third year Zishang moved his garrison to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zishang moved his garrison to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 遷撫軍長史，行府州事。

translations.literal: Huaiwen was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army, handling the prince's prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen became pacification-army chief clerk and handled the prince's prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 時囚系甚多，動經年月，懷文到任，訊五郡九百三十六獄，眾咸稱平。

translations.literal: At that time prisoners were very many and often held for years; when Huaiwen took office he tried cases in five commanderies—nine hundred thirty-six prisons—and all praised the fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were many and often held for years; Huaiwen tried nine hundred thirty-six cases in five commanderies and all praised the fairness.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中，寵待隆密。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attendant and was favored intimately and closely.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as attendant and was favored closely.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵反，及城陷，士庶皆裸身鞭面然後加刑，聚所殺人首于石頭南岸，謂之髑髏山。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Jingling held Guangling in rebellion and the city fell, gentry and commoners were all stripped naked and whipped on the face before punishment; the heads of those killed were piled on the south bank of Stone City—called Skull Mountain.
