translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled at Guangling and the city fell, people were stripped and whipped before execution; heads piled on Stone City's south bank were called Skull Mountain.

sentences.zh: 懷文陳其不可，上不納。

translations.literal: Huaiwen stated that this could not be; the emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said this was wrong; the emperor did not accept.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘗有事圓丘，未至期而雨晦竟夜。

translations.literal: The Filial Emperor once was to perform the round-mound rite; before the date rain and gloom lasted the whole night.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu was to perform the round-mound rite; rain and gloom lasted the whole night before the date.

sentences.zh: 明旦風霽，雲色甚美，帝升壇悅。

translations.literal: At dawn the wind cleared; the clouds were very beautiful; the emperor ascended the altar in joy.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the wind cleared and clouds were beautiful; the emperor ascended the altar in joy.

sentences.zh: 懷文稱慶曰：「昔漢後郊祀太一，白日重輪，神光四燭。

translations.literal: Huaiwen spoke congratulation, saying, "In the past Han's later emperor sacrificed to the Grand Unity and the sun doubled its wheel and divine light shone on four sides."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen congratulated him: "When Han's later emperor sacrificed to the Grand Unity, the sun doubled its wheel and divine light shone on four sides."

sentences.zh: 今陛下有事茲禮，而膏雨迎夜，清景麗朝，斯實聖明幽感所致，臣願與侍臣賦之。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty performs this rite, and moist rain welcomed the night and clear scenery adorned the morning—this is truly reached by the sage's hidden resonance; your servant wishes to compose a fu with the attendants."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty performs this rite; moist rain came by night and clear skies at dawn—surely the sage's hidden resonance; I wish to compose a fu with the attendants."

sentences.zh: 」上笑稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and praised it.

sentences.zh: 揚州移會稽，上忿浙江東人情不和，欲貶其勞祿，唯西州舊人不改。

translations.literal: When Yangzhou moved to Kuaiji the emperor resented that the people east of the Zhe River were not harmonious and wished to reduce their salaries and emoluments; only old Western Province men were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou moved to Kuaiji the emperor resented discord east of the Zhe and wished to cut salaries; only old Western Province men were spared.

sentences.zh: 懷文曰：「揚州徙居，既乖人情，一州兩格，尤失大體。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "Moving Yangzhou already goes against sentiment; two standards in one province especially loses the larger principle."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "Moving Yangzhou already offends hearts; two standards in one province loses the larger principle."

sentences.zh: 」上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 懷文與顏竣、周朗素善，竣以失旨見誅，朗亦以忤意得罪。

translations.literal: Huaiwen was on good terms with Yan Jun and Zhou Lang; Jun was executed for losing favor and Lang also offended and was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen was close to Yan Jun and Zhou Lang; Jun was executed for losing favor and Lang also offended and was punished.

sentences.zh: 上謂懷文曰：「竣若知我殺之，亦當不敢如此。

translations.literal: The emperor told Huaiwen, "If Jun had known I would kill him, he would not have dared be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Huaiwen, "If Jun had known I would kill him, he would not have dared act so."

sentences.zh: 」懷文默然。

translations.literal: Huaiwen was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen was silent.

sentences.zh: 又嘗以歲夕與謝莊、王景文、顏師伯被敕入省，未及進，景文因談言次稱竣、朗人才之美，懷文與相酬和。

translations.literal: Once on New Year's Eve he was ordered into the Secretariat with Xie Zhuang, Wang Jingwen, and Yan Shibo before entering; on the way Jingwen in conversation praised the talent of Jun and Lang, and Huaiwen responded in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Once on New Year's Eve he was ordered into the Secretariat with Zhuang, Jingwen, and Shibo; Jingwen praised Jun and Lang and Huaiwen agreed.

sentences.zh: 師伯後因語次白上，敘景文等此言。

translations.literal: Shibo later in conversation told the emperor and reported Jingwen's words.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo later told the emperor what Jingwen had said.

sentences.zh: 懷文屢經犯忤，至此上倍不悅。

translations.literal: Huaiwen had repeatedly offended; now the emperor was doubly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen had repeatedly offended; now the emperor was doubly displeased.

sentences.zh: 上又壞諸郡士族以充將吏，並不服役，至悉逃亡。

translations.literal: The emperor also broke up gentry clans of the commanderies to fill general and official posts; none would serve corvée and all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also drafted gentry clans to fill posts; none would serve corvée and all fled.

sentences.zh: 加以嚴制不能禁，乃改用軍法，得便斬之。

translations.literal: Adding strict rules could not forbid it; then military law was used and offenders could be beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Strict rules could not stop it; military law was used and offenders could be beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 莫不奔竄山湖，聚為盜賊。

translations.literal: None did not flee into mountains and lakes and gather as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: All fled into mountains and lakes and became bandits.

sentences.zh: 懷文又以為言。

translations.literal: Huaiwen again spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen spoke on this again.

sentences.zh: 齋庫上絹年調钜萬疋，綿亦稱此，期限嚴峻。

translations.literal: Silk for the palace stores in the annual levy reached tens of thousands of bolts; cotton likewise; the deadline was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Silk for palace stores in the annual levy reached tens of thousands of bolts, cotton likewise; deadlines were severe.

sentences.zh: 人間買絹一疋至三二千，綿一兩三四百，貧者賣妻子，甚者或自縊死。

translations.literal: Among the people one bolt of silk cost two or three thousand and one liang of cotton three or four hundred; the poor sold wives and children, and some hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Silk cost two or three thousand per bolt and cotton three or four hundred per liang; the poor sold wives and children, some hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 懷文具陳人困，由是綿絹薄有所減，俄復舊。

translations.literal: Huaiwen fully stated the people's distress; thereby silk and cotton were slightly reduced, but soon returned to the old amount.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen stated the people's distress; silk and cotton were slightly reduced, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 子尚等諸皇子皆置邸舍，逐什一之利，為患遍天下。

translations.literal: Zishang and other princes all set up lodges and pursued one-tenth profit—the harm spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zishang and other princes set up lodges for one-tenth profit—the harm spread through the realm.

sentences.zh: 懷文又曰：「列肆販賣，古人所非。

translations.literal: Huaiwen again said, "Setting out stalls to sell—what the ancients rejected."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said again, "Setting out stalls to sell is what the ancients rejected."

sentences.zh: 卜式明不雨之由，弘羊受致旱之責。

translations.literal: Bu Shi clarified the reason for no rain; Hong Yang bore blame for causing drought.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Shi explained drought's cause; Hong Yang bore blame for causing it.

sentences.zh: 若以用度不充，故宜量加減省。

translations.literal: If expenditure is insufficient, one should measure increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: If expenditure falls short, measure increase and decrease.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，抑黜諸弟，廣陵平後，復欲更峻其科。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian the younger brothers had been suppressed; after Guangling was pacified he wished to tighten the code further.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaojian younger brothers had been suppressed; after Guangling was pacified he wished to tighten the code.

sentences.zh: 懷文曰：「漢明不使其子比光武之子，前史以為美談。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "Han Ming did not let his sons compare with Guangwu's sons—the former histories praised this as fine talk."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "Han Ming did not let his sons compare with Guangwu's—the histories praised this."

sentences.zh: 陛下既明管、蔡之誅，願崇唐、衛之寄。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already clarified the punishment of Guan and Cai; I wish you would honor the entrustment of Tang and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has clarified Guan and Cai's punishment; honor the entrustment of Tang and Wei."

sentences.zh: 」及海陵王休茂誅，欲遂前議。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiumao of Hailing was executed he wished to pursue the earlier discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiumao of Hailing was executed he wished to pursue the earlier discussion.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭探得密旨，先發議端，懷文固請不可，由是得息。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Yixong of Jiangxia obtained the secret intent and first opened the discussion; Huaiwen firmly asked that it not be done, and by this it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yixong obtained the secret intent and opened the discussion; Huaiwen firmly objected and it ceased.

sentences.zh: 時游幸無度，太后六宮常乘副車在後。

translations.literal: At that time touring was without limit; the empress dowager and the six palaces often rode escort carriages behind.
translations.idiomatic: Touring was then without limit; the empress dowager and six palaces often rode escort carriages behind.

sentences.zh: 懷文與王景文每諫不宜亟出，後因從坐松樹下，風雨甚驟。

translations.literal: Huaiwen and Wang Jingwen often remonstrated that one should not go out so often; later, sitting under pines, wind and rain came fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen and Jingwen often remonstrated against going out so often; later sitting under pines, wind and rain came fiercely.

sentences.zh: 景文曰：「卿可以言矣。

translations.literal: Jingwen said, "You may speak now."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen said, "You may speak now."

sentences.zh: 」懷文曰：「獨言無繼，宜相與陳之。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "Speaking alone has no follow— we should state it together."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "Alone I have no follow—we should speak together."

sentences.zh: 」江智深臥草側，亦謂之善。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhishen lay on the grass beside them and also called it good.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhishen, lying on the grass nearby, also approved.

sentences.zh: 俄而被召俱入雉場，懷文曰：「風雨如此，非聖躬所宜。

translations.literal: Soon all were summoned into the pheasant field; Huaiwen said, "Wind and rain like this are not fit for Your Sacred Person."
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were summoned to the pheasant field; Huaiwen said, "Weather like this is not fit for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」景文又曰：「懷文所啟宜從。

translations.literal: Jingwen also said, "What Huaiwen memorializes should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen added, "Huaiwen's words should be followed."

sentences.zh: 」智深未及有言，上方注弩，作色曰：「卿欲效顏竣邪？

translations.literal: Zhishen had not yet spoken when the emperor, fixing his crossbow, changed color and said, "Do you wish to imitate Yan Jun?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhishen could speak the emperor, fixing his crossbow, darkened: "Do you imitate Yan Jun?"

sentences.zh: 何以恒知人事。

translations.literal: Why do you always know human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you always know human affairs?

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「顏竣小子，恨不得鞭其面。」

translations.literal: He also said, "That boy Yan Jun—I wish I could whip his face."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "That boy Jun—I wish I could whip his face."

sentences.zh: 上每宴集，在坐者咸令沈醉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor held banquets those seated were all ordered drunk.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets those seated were all ordered drunk.

sentences.zh: 懷文素不飲酒，又不好戲，上謂故欲異己。

translations.literal: Huaiwen never drank and also disliked games; the emperor thought he deliberately wished to differ.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen never drank and disliked games; the emperor thought he deliberately differed.

sentences.zh: 謝莊嘗誡懷文曰：「卿每與人異，亦何可久。

translations.literal: Xie Zhuang once admonished Huaiwen, "You always differ from others—how can it last long?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhuang once warned him, "You always differ from others—how can that last?"

sentences.zh: 」懷文曰：「吾少來如此，豈可一朝而變。

translations.literal: Huaiwen said, "I have been thus from youth—how can I change in a morning?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen said, "I have been thus from youth—how change in a morning?"

sentences.zh: 非欲異物，性之所不能耳。」

translations.literal: It is not that I wish to differ from things—it is what my nature cannot do."
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish to differ—it is what my nature cannot do."

sentences.zh: 五年，出為晉安王子勳征虜長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as Chief Clerk of the Punitive Army under Prince Zixun of Jin'an and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he went out as punitive-army chief clerk under Prince Zixun of Jin'an and Guangling administrator.

sentences.zh: 明帝坐朝正事畢，被遣還北，以女病求申，臨辭又乞停三日，訖猶不去，為有司所糾，免官，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming sat court and finished regular business he was sent back north; citing his daughter's illness he asked delay; at parting he again begged three days' stop, and when done still did not leave— impeached by the authorities, removed from office, and confined for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming finished court business he was sent north; citing his daughter's illness he delayed; at parting he begged three days more and still did not leave—impeached, removed, and confined ten years.

sentences.zh: 既被免，賣宅還東。

translations.literal: Once removed he sold his house and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Once removed he sold his house and returned east.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，收付廷尉賜死。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, arrested him, and handed him to the court for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, arrested him, and had him executed by the court.

sentences.zh: 弟懷遠為始興王浚征北長流參軍，深見親待。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huaiyuan was Senior Clerk of the Northern Army under Prince Jun of Shixing and was deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Huaiyuan was northern-army senior clerk under Prince Jun of Shixing and was deeply favored.

sentences.zh: 坐納王鸚鵡為妾，孝武徙之廣州。

translations.literal: For taking Wang Yingwu as concubine the Filial Emperor exiled him to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For taking Yingwu as concubine Xiaowu exiled him to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史宗愨欲殺之，會南郡王義宣反，懷遠頗閑文筆，愨起義，使造檄書，並銜命至始興，與始興相沈法系論起義事。

translations.literal: Inspector Zong Que wished to kill him; when Prince Yixuan of Nanjun rebelled Huaiyuan was fairly skilled with the brush; Que raised the righteous banner and had him draft proclamations and also sent him with orders to Shixing to discuss the uprising with Administrator Shen Faxi.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zong Que wished to kill him; when Prince Yixuan of Nanjun rebelled Huaiyuan, skilled with the brush, drafted proclamations for Que and went to Shixing to discuss the uprising with Shen Faxi.

sentences.zh: 事平，愨具為陳請，由此見原。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled Que fully petitioned on his behalf and by this he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled Que fully petitioned for him and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 終孝武世不得還。

translations.literal: Through the Filial Emperor's age he was not permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: Through Xiaowu's reign he was not permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝世歸，位武康令，撰南越志，及懷文文集並傳於世。

translations.literal: In the Deposed Emperor's age he returned, reached Magistrate of Wukang, compiled the Record of the Southern Yue, and his collected writings with Huaiwen's circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he returned, became magistrate of Wukang, compiled the Record of the Southern Yue, and his and Huaiwen's writings circulated.

sentences.zh: 懷文三子：淡、深、沖。

translations.literal: Huaiwen had three sons: Dan, Shen, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen had three sons: Dan, Shen, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖字景綽，涉獵文義，仕宋歷位撫軍正佐，兼記室。

translations.literal: Chong, courtesy name Jingchuo, ranged through letters and meaning and in Song reached Regular Assistant to the Pacification Army, concurrently Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Jingchuo, ranged through letters and meaning and reached regular assistant to the pacification army and recorder.

sentences.zh: 及懷文得罪被系，沖兄弟行謝，情哀貌苦，見者傷之。

translations.literal: When Huaiwen was guilty and imprisoned Chong and his brothers went to apologize—their grief in feeling and face moved those who saw them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiwen was imprisoned Chong and his brothers went to apologize; their grief moved all who saw them.

sentences.zh: 柳元景欲救懷文，言于孝武曰：「沈懷文三子塗炭不可見，願陛下速正其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "He should be killed quickly so that his mind may divide."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Kill him quickly so his mind may divide."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「宜急殺之，使其意分。

translations.literal: In the end they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they were killed.

sentences.zh: 」竟殺之。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sighed for them; the Chong brothers became famous by this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing sighed; the Chong brothers became famous by this.

sentences.zh: 元景為之歎息，沖兄弟以此知名。

translations.literal: Chong was repeatedly promoted to Recorder of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Chong rose to recorder of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 累遷司徒錄事。

translations.literal: The censor's duty of impeachment—many who were indicted bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The censor's duty of impeachment—many indicted bore resentment.

sentences.zh: 中丞案裁之職，被惡者多結怨。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era Shen impeached Administrator of Wuxing Yuan Luan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming Shen impeached Wuxing administrator Yuan Luan.

sentences.zh: 永明中，深彈吳興太守袁彖。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era Luan's cousin Ang was Censor-in-Chief; within days of taking office he memorialized to impeach Shen's son Hui for his father's renting a white-canopied cart while living and removed him from office with confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu Luan's cousin Ang became censor-in-chief; within days he impeached Shen's son Hui for renting a white-canopied cart during his father's life and removed him with confinement.

sentences.zh: 建武中，彖從弟昂為中丞，到官數日，奏彈深子繢父在僦白幰車，免官禁錮。

translations.literal: Chong's mother Lady Kong was in the east; a neighbor's house caught fire and she suspected arson, crying loudly, "All three of my sons have been censor-in-chief—can they have done good to anyone?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong's mother Lady Kong was in the east; a neighbor's house burned and she cried, "All three sons were censor-in-chief—did they ever do anyone good?"

sentences.zh: 沖母孔氏在東，鄰家失火，疑為人所焚爇，大呼曰：「我三兒皆作御史中丞，與人豈有善者。

translations.literal: I fear flesh divided and bones scattered—how much less mere burning.
translations.idiomatic: I fear flesh divided and bones scattered—how much less mere burning.

sentences.zh: 方恐肌分骨散，何但焚如。

translations.literal: The brothers later all served as attendants; Emperor Wu was about to employ Chong when he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers later all served as attendants; Emperor Wu was about to employ Chong when he died.

sentences.zh: 」兄弟後並曆侍中，武帝方欲任沖，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies with the posthumous title Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of ceremonies with the posthumous title Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 追贈太常，諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: Tanqing was Huaiwen's father's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing was Huaiwen's father's elder brother's son.

sentences.zh: 曇慶，懷文從父兄也。

translations.literal: His father Fa was Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fa was supernumerary attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 父發，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Tanqing served in Song and reached Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing served in Song and reached left assistant director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曇慶仕宋位尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In years of flood and drought Tanqing proposed establishing a Ever-Normal Granary to save people in emergency; Emperor Wen accepted the words but the affair was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In flood and drought years Tanqing proposed an ever-normal granary to save people in emergency; Wen accepted but did not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 時歲有水旱，曇慶議立常平倉以救人急，文帝納其言而事不行。

translations.literal: Tanqing was cautious, solid, and clear; wherever he served had praised achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing was cautious, solid, and clear; wherever he served won praise.

sentences.zh: 曇慶謹實清正，所蒞有稱績。

translations.literal: He often told his sons and younger brothers, "I have no talent in dealing with the world—I only aim to be a great old man."
translations.idiomatic: He often told his kin, "I have no worldly talent—I only aim to be a great old man."

sentences.zh: 常謂子弟曰：「吾處世無才能，圖作大老子耳。

translations.literal: The age called him an elder.
translations.idiomatic: The age called him an elder.

sentences.zh: 」世以長者稱之。

translations.literal: He died as Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died as minister of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 卒于祠部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhou Lang, courtesy name Yili, was a native of Ancheng in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang, styled Yili, came from Ancheng in Runan.

sentences.zh: 周朗字義利，汝南安成人也。

translations.literal: His father Chun in the early Song reached Attendant and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun in early Song reached attendant and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父淳，宋初歷位侍中，太常。

translations.literal: His elder brother Qiao married Emperor Wu's fourth daughter, Princess Dexuan of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qiao married Emperor Wu's fourth daughter, Princess Dexuan of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 兄嶠尚武帝第四女宣城德公主。

translations.literal: Two daughters married Prince Hong of Jianping and Prince Hui of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters married Prince Hong of Jianping and Prince Hui of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 二女適建平王宏、廬江王褘。

translations.literal: By imperial kinship they held illustrious office.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial kinship they held illustrious office.

sentences.zh: 以貴戚顯官。

translations.literal: Lang from youth loved the unusual and had an elegant air; his aims differed from Qiao's and Qiao greatly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Lang from youth loved the unusual and had elegant air; his aims differed from Qiao's and Qiao resented him.

sentences.zh: 朗少而愛奇，雅有風氣，與嶠志趨不同，嶠甚疾之。

translations.literal: He served as Army Aide to Grand Marshal Prince Yixong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He served as army aide to Grand Marshal Prince Yixong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 為江夏王義恭太尉參軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia court discussed northern invasion of Wei; Prince Yixong was to go out to garrison Pengcheng as supreme commander of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 27 spring court debated invading Wei north; Prince Yixong was to garrison Pengcheng as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年春，朝議北侵魏，當遣義恭出鎮彭城，為諸軍大統。

translations.literal: Lang heard and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Lang heard and resigned.

sentences.zh: 朗聞之解職。

translations.literal: When Yixong went out to garrison, Chief Clerk Yang Xi of the headquarters went with him and in a playful letter to Lang urged him to offer extraordinary plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixong garrisoned Pengcheng, chief clerk Yang Xi wrote playfully urging Lang to offer extraordinary plans.

sentences.zh: 及義恭出鎮，府主簿羊希從行，與朗書戲之，勸令獻奇進策。

translations.literal: Lang replied citing ancient precedent; the language was free and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Lang replied citing ancient precedent in free, bold language.

sentences.zh: 朗報書援引古義，辭意倜儻。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Luling; the commandery borders were desolate and there were many wild beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Luling administrator; the borders were desolate and wild beasts many.

sentences.zh: 後為廬陵內史，郡界荒蕪，頗有野獸。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Xue wished to see a hunt; Lang then closed the ring and set fire, letting his mother watch.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Xue wished to see a hunt; Lang closed the ring, set fire, and let her watch.

sentences.zh: 母薛氏欲見獵，朗乃合圍縱火，令母觀之。

translations.literal: The fire escaped and burned the commandery offices; Lang fully used his salary grain to build houses and compensate the burned limit.
translations.idiomatic: Fire escaped and burned the yamen; Lang used his salary grain to rebuild and compensate.

sentences.zh: 火逸燒郡解，朗悉以秩米起屋，償所燒之限。

translations.literal: Claiming illness he left office; impeached by the provincial inspector, he returned to the capital and told Emperor Xiaowu, "The provincial inspector's listing of my faults is largely not justified; in the commandery wild beasts three times ate people and insects and rats harmed the crops—for these two matters I fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Claiming illness he left; impeached by the inspector, he told Xiaowu, "Most charges are unjust; wild beasts ate three people and pests harmed crops—for these I fail Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 稱疾去官，為州司所糾，還都謝孝武曰：「州司舉臣愆失多不允，臣在郡猛獸三食人，蟲鼠犯稼，以此二事上負陛下。

translations.literal: The emperor's face changed and said, "The provincial inspector's disapproval may exist."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed: "The inspector's disapproval may exist."

sentences.zh: 」上變色曰：「州司不允，或可有之。

translations.literal: Disaster from insects and beasts—how does it concern your small matter?"
translations.idiomatic: Insect and beast disaster—what has that to do with you?"

sentences.zh: 蟲獸之災，甯關卿小物。」

translations.literal: Lang soon entered mourning for his mother; each time he wept he was convulsed with grief, yet otherwise he largely did not follow the usual mourning rules.
translations.idiomatic: Lang soon mourned his mother; each weeping convulsed him, yet otherwise he largely ignored usual mourning rules.

sentences.zh: 朗尋丁母憂，每哭必慟，其餘頗不依居喪常節。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming the emperor had the authorities memorialize his mourning without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 4 the emperor had authorities memorialize his improper mourning.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，上使有司奏其居喪無禮。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Lang is contrary to rites and glib—he should be cut down and killed; this small man is not worth disturbing the standard punishments— specially lock and send to a frontier commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Lang is contrary to rites and glib—fit for execution; this small man is not worth disturbing punishments—send him to the frontier."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朗悖禮利口，宜合翦戮，微物不足亂典刑，特鎖付邊郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent to Ning Province and killed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Ning Province and killed on the road.

sentences.zh: 」於是傳送甯州，於道殺之。

translations.literal: Lang's clansman grandson Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's clansman grandson Yong.

sentences.zh: 朗族孫顒。

translations.literal: Yong, courtesy name Yanlun, was seventh-generation descendant of Yan, Left Director of Splendid Honors in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, styled Yanlun, was seventh-generation descendant of Yan, Jin's left director of splendid honors.

sentences.zh: 顒字彥倫，晉左光祿大夫顗七世孫也。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hutou was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hutou was supernumerary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 祖虎頭，員外常侍。

translations.literal: His father Xun was District Administrator of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun was district administrator of Guixiang.

sentences.zh: 父恂，歸鄉相。

translations.literal: Yong in youth was known to his clansman elder Lang; he left the hempen and became Gentleman of Hailing Principality.
translations.idiomatic: Yong in youth was known to Lang; he left the hempen and became gentleman of Hailing principality.

sentences.zh: 顒少為族祖朗所知，解褐海陵國侍郎。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Xiao Hui Kai prized Yong and took him into Shu, making him General of Fierce Edge, concurrently Magistrate of Feixiang and Chengdu, still Chief Clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou inspector Xiao Hui Kai prized Yong, took him to Shu, made him general of fierce edge and magistrate of Feixiang and Chengdu, still headquarters chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史蕭惠開賞異顒，攜入蜀，為厲鋒將軍，帶肥鄉、成都二縣令，仍為府主簿。

translations.literal: He often told Hui Kai his nature was too dangerous; he often remonstrated and Hui Kai was displeased and replied to Yong, "Heaven's danger, earth's danger—lords set danger; one need only ask how danger is used."
translations.idiomatic: He often told Hui Kai his nature was too dangerous; remonstrating often, he earned the reply, "Heaven's danger, earth's danger—lords set danger; ask only how it is used."

sentences.zh: 常謂惠開性太險，每致諫，惠開不悅，答顒曰：「天險地險，王侯設險，但問用險何如耳。

translations.literal: He followed Hui Kai back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hui Kai back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」隨惠開還都。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song quite loved arcane principle; because Yong had eloquent meaning he was brought into the palace hall and kept close on night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming loved arcane learning; Yong's eloquence brought him into the palace on night duty.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝頗好玄理，以顒有辭義，引入殿內，親近宿直。

translations.literal: For cruel deeds the emperor performed Yong did not dare remonstrate openly but would recite scriptural stories of cause and effect and guilt and blessing; the emperor too would slightly stop.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor's cruel deeds Yong did not dare remonstrate openly but recited scriptural tales of cause and effect; the emperor slightly stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝所為慘毒之事，顒不敢顯諫，輒誦經中因緣罪福事，帝亦為之小止。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was ordered to be Magistrate of Shan; he had kindness and the people missed him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui he was magistrate of Shan; kind, he was missed by the people.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，詔為剡令，有恩惠，百姓思之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted government he was Attendant of the Qi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted government he was Qi palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，為齊殿中郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan he was Rear Army Aide to the Prince of Changsha and Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyuan's start he was rear-army aide to the Prince of Changsha and Shanyin magistrate.

sentences.zh: 建元初，為長沙王后軍參軍、山陰令。

translations.literal: He returned as Recorder of the Central Army under Crown Prince Wen Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as central-army recorder under Crown Prince Wen Hui.

sentences.zh: 還為文惠太子中軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Wen Hui was in the Eastern Palace Yong was promoted to Regular Gentleman, Front Army Adviser to Prince of Shixing, attending directly in the palace hall, deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Hui was heir, Yong became regular gentleman and front-army adviser to Prince of Shixing, attending in the palace, deeply favored.

sentences.zh: 文惠在東宮，顒遷正員郎，始興王前軍諮議，直侍殿省，深見賞遇。

translations.literal: Yong's speech was eloquent and beautiful; he excelled in Buddhist principle and wrote the Treatise on the Three Teachings on the meaning of emptiness and provision.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's speech was eloquent; he excelled in Buddhist principle and wrote the Treatise on the Three Teachings on emptiness and provision.

sentences.zh: 顒音辭辯麗，長於佛理，著三宗論言空假義。

translations.literal: The monk Zhilin of Western Liangzhou sent Yong a letter deeply praising him, saying, "Holding a fly-whisk for more than forty years I have seen many sect records; in this path black and white have not one who attained it—it makes me ill; I did not expect this sound rudely to enter the ear."
translations.idiomatic: Monk Zhilin of Western Liangzhou wrote praising him: "Forty years with fly-whisk in hand I have seen sect records; on this path none attained—I did not expect this voice in my ear."

sentences.zh: 西涼州智林道人遺顒書深相讚美，言：「捉麈尾來四十餘載，頗見宗錄，唯此塗白黑無一人得者，為之發病，非意此音猥來入耳」。

translations.literal: His treatise was valued to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: His treatise was valued to this degree.

sentences.zh: 其論見重如此。

translations.literal: Yong established a hermitage west of Mount Zhong and on rest days returned there.
translations.idiomatic: Yong built a hermitage west of Mount Zhong and returned on rest days.

sentences.zh: 顒於鍾山西立隱舍，休沐則歸之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Steward of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Compiler, compiling the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He became steward of the heir apparent and compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 轉太子僕，兼著作，撰起居注。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Secretariat, still Compiler as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat gentleman, still compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，兼著作如故。

translations.literal: He often attended and served in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He often attended in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 常遊侍東宮。

translations.literal: In youth from his maternal uncle's house, General of Chariots and Cavalry Zang Zhi's family, he obtained Wei Heng's draft clerical script and studied it very skillfully.
translations.idiomatic: In youth at his maternal uncle General Zang Zhi's house he obtained Wei Heng's draft clerical script and mastered it.

sentences.zh: 少從外氏車騎將軍臧質家得衛恒散隸書法，學之甚工。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wen Hui had Yong write on the wall of the Mystic Garden thatched studio.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wen Hui had Yong write on the Mystic Garden thatched studio wall.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子使顒書玄圃茅齋壁。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial University He Yin sought to exchange inverted-leek script with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial University director He Yin sought to exchange inverted-leek script with Yong.

translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu Wu Bao of Wei returned south with Confucian learning.

translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang Shi invited Bao to lecture; She refuted him with forceful elegant reasoning and was famed for debate.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang as Danyang administrator recruited him as chief clerk and entrusted many affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞。

translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Minister of Ceremonies.

translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu ascended, Fan Yun valued She and spoke to the emperor; he was summoned as gentleman of the temples section.

sentences.zh: 禮儀損益，多自舍出。

translations.literal: Ritual increase and decrease largely came from She.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual changes largely came from She.

sentences.zh: 累遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the court for dependencies.

translations.idiomatic: When Wang Liang was guilty and returned home no friend came; only She treated old kindness.

sentences.zh: 及亮卒，身營殯葬，時人稱之。

translations.literal: When Liang died She personally arranged burial; men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang died She arranged burial; men praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，太子右衛率，右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Personnel of the Masters of Writing, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of personnel, right commandant of the heir's guard, and general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 雖居職屢徙，而常留省內，罕得休下。

translations.literal: Though his office changed repeatedly he always remained in the Secretariat and rarely had rest below.
translations.idiomatic: Though offices changed he always remained in the Secretariat and rarely rested.

sentences.zh: 國史詔誥，儀體法律，軍旅謀謨，皆兼掌之。

translations.literal: National history, edicts and proclamations, ritual forms and laws, military counsel—all were concurrently managed.
translations.idiomatic: National history, edicts, ritual, military counsel—all were concurrently managed.

sentences.zh: 日夜侍上，豫機密二十餘年，未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Day and night he attended the emperor; for more than twenty years he handled secrets and never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he attended; for twenty years he handled secrets and never left the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 帝以為有公輔器。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him to have the vessel of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered him fit for chief minister.

translations.literal: At first when Fan Yun died all considered Shen Yue fit for the pivot; the emperor held Yue lighter than Xu Mian and so Mian and She jointly shared state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yun died all considered Shen Yue fit for power; the emperor held Yue lighter than Xu Mian and Mian and She shared state affairs.

translations.literal: Mian was removed for a small resentment; She alone held power; his magnanimity did not reach Mian's yet his clarity and simplicity surpassed him—both were called worthy chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was removed for small resentment; She alone held power—less magnanimous than Mian yet clearer; both were called worthy chancellors.

translations.idiomatic: Discussion of national history then doubted Emperor Wen's annals and biography.

translations.idiomatic: He used reed screens; when broken he did not repair.

translations.idiomatic: In prison he presented a martial poem to Emperor Wu; pardoned he returned to his post.

translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng was broadly learned, knew omens, and divined skillfully.

translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell Hongzheng fawned on Wang Wei, joined clan with Zhou Shizhen, changed surname to Ji to avoid Jing's taboo, and was made minister of ceremonies.

translations.idiomatic: When Jing was about to usurp he managed ritual.

translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian marched east Emperor Yuan asked, "Which court gentleman comes first?"

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian said, "Surely Zhou Hongzheng."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian said, "Surely Zhou Hongzheng."

sentences.zh: 」王僧辯曰：「其周弘正乎。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian said, "Surely Zhou Hongzheng."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian said, "Surely Zhou Hongzheng."

sentences.zh: 弘正智不後機，體能濟勝，無妻子之顧，有獨決之明，其餘碌碌不逮也。

translations.literal: Hongzheng's wit does not lag behind opportunity; his person can overcome difficulty; he has no concern for wife and children and has the clarity of solitary decision—the rest are dull and do not reach him."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng's wit does not lag; his person overcomes difficulty; no wife and children to worry him and solitary clarity—the rest do not reach him."

sentences.zh: 」俄而前部傳云弘正至，僧辯飛騎迎之。

translations.literal: Soon the vanguard reported Hongzheng had arrived; Sengbian flew horse to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the vanguard reported Hongzheng arrived; Sengbian flew horse to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 及見，歡甚，曰：「吾固知王僧達非後機者，公可坐吾膝上。

translations.literal: On meeting he was very pleased and said, "I knew Wang Sengbian was not one to lag behind opportunity—you may sit on my knee."
translations.idiomatic: Meeting he was pleased: "I knew Sengbian does not lag—you may sit on my knee."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「可謂進而若將加諸膝，老夫何足以當。

translations.literal: He replied, "One may say advancing as if about to place on the knee—this old man is not enough to bear it."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Advancing as if to place on the knee—this old man cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 」僧辯即日啟元帝，元帝手書與弘正，仍遣使迎之，謂朝士曰：「晉氏平吳，喜獲二陸，今我討賊，亦得兩周。

translations.literal: Sengbian that day memorialized Emperor Yuan; Yuan wrote personally to Hongzheng and still sent envoys to welcome him, telling court gentlemen, "When Jin pacified Wu they were glad to gain the two Lus; now in punishing the rebel we also gain the two Zhous."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian memorialized Yuan; Yuan wrote Hongzheng and sent envoys, telling court, "Jin pacifying Wu gained the two Lus; punishing the rebel we gain the two Zhous."

sentences.zh: 」及至，禮數甚優，朝臣無比。

translations.literal: When he arrived ritual was very generous—no court gentleman compared.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived ritual was generous—no court gentleman compared.

sentences.zh: 授黃門侍郎，直侍中省。

translations.literal: He was given Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, attending directly in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was given attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, attending in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄遷左戶尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Minister of the Household and given concurrent Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon left minister of the household and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 夏月著犢鼻褌，衣朱衣，為有司所彈。

translations.literal: In summer he wore calf-nose breeches and vermilion robes and was impeached by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he wore calf-nose breeches and vermilion robes and was impeached.

sentences.zh: 其放達如此。

translations.literal: He was so free and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He was so free and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 元帝嘗著金樓子，曰：「余于諸僧重招提琰法師，隱士重華陽陶貞白，士大夫重汝南周弘正，其于義理清轉無窮，亦一時之名士也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan once wrote the Golden Tower Master, saying, "Among monks I value Abbot Yan of Zhaoti; among recluses I value Tao Zhenbai of Huayang; among gentry I value Zhou Hongzheng of Runan—for clarity and turning of principle without end, he too is a famous scholar of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote the Golden Tower Master: "Among monks I value Abbot Yan; among recluses Tao Zhenbai; among gentry Zhou Hongzheng of Runan—clarity and turning of principle without end, a famous scholar of the age."

sentences.zh: 弘正善清談，梁末為玄宗之冠。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was skilled at pure talk and at the end of Liang was crown of the arcane school.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng was skilled at pure talk and at Liang's end was crown of the arcane school.

sentences.zh: 及侯景平，僧辯啟送秘府圖籍，敕弘正讎校。

translations.literal: At that time court discussed moving the capital; but Yuan had twice presided over Jing and Shan for more than twenty years and emotionally clung and did not wish to return to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussed moving the capital; Yuan had presided over Jing and Shan twenty years and clung there, unwilling to return to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時朝議遷都，但元帝再臨荊陝，前後二十餘年，情所安戀，不欲歸建業。

translations.literal: Moreover the old headquarters staff were all men of Chu and all wished at once to make the capital Jiangling, saying, "Jiankang is indeed the old capital but desolation is already extreme."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover old headquarters staff were Chu men and wished to make Jiangling capital: "Jiankang is the old capital but desolation is extreme."

sentences.zh: 兼故府臣僚皆楚人，並欲即都江陵，云：「建康蓋是舊都，雕荒已極。

translations.literal: Moreover royal qi is already exhausted; moreover separated from the north by one river—if there is misfortune there is no time for regret."
translations.idiomatic: Royal qi is exhausted; we are separated from the north by one river—if misfortune comes regret is too late."

sentences.zh: 且王氣已盡，兼與北止隔一江，若有不虞，悔無所及。

translations.literal: Moreover your servants also hear that south of the Jing there is emperor's qi—now it has answered."
translations.idiomatic: We also hear emperor's qi south of the Jing—now it has answered."

sentences.zh: 且臣等又聞荊南有天子氣，今其應矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan had no intent to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan had no intent to leave.

sentences.zh: 」元帝無去意。

translations.literal: At that time Left Vice Director Wang Bao and Hongzheng both attended; the emperor looked and said, "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Bao and Hongzheng attended; the emperor asked, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 時尚書左僕射王褒及弘正咸侍，帝顧曰：「卿意何如？

translations.literal: Bao and the others because the emperor was suspicious did not dare state public harm in the assembly and only assented.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and others, knowing the emperor's suspicion, did not dare speak openly and only assented.

sentences.zh: 」褒等以帝猜忌，弗敢眾中公害，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Bao later in a quiet moment secretly remonstrated to return to Danyang very forcefully; though the emperor accepted it his face was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Bao later in quiet secretly remonstrated to return to Danyang forcefully; the emperor accepted but his face was displeased.

sentences.zh: 褒後因清閒，密諫還丹陽甚切，帝雖納之，色不悅。

translations.literal: On the next day in the assembly he told Bao, "Yesterday you urged return to Jiankang—not without reason; I thought on it last night and still harbor doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Next day in assembly he told Bao, "Yesterday you urged Jiankang—not without reason; I thought last night and still doubt."

sentences.zh: 及明日，眾中謂褒曰：「卿昨勸還建鄴，不為無理，吾昨夜思之，猶懷疑惑。

translations.literal: Bao knew he would not be adopted and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bao knew he would not be heeded and stopped.

sentences.zh: 」褒知不引納，乃止。

translations.literal: Another day Hongzheng remonstrated with stern face to the point of three repetitions, saying, "If like the gentry and officials, wherever the sage king dwells there is no fixed place."
translations.idiomatic: Another day Hongzheng remonstrated sternly thrice: "For gentry and officials the sage king's seat has no fixed place."

sentences.zh: 他日，弘正乃正色諫，至於再三，曰：「若如士大夫，唯聖王所都，本無定處。

translations.literal: As for the common people, not yet seeing entry into Jiankang city they then say it is not yet the Son of Heaven but still the feudal kings of the states."
translations.idiomatic: But common people not yet seeing entry into Jiankang say he is not yet Son of Heaven but still a feudal king."

sentences.zh: 至如黔首，未見入建鄴城，便謂未是天子，猶列國諸王。

translations.literal: Today to follow the people's hearts one cannot but return to Jiankang."
translations.idiomatic: Today to follow the people's hearts one must return to Jiankang."

sentences.zh: 今日赴百姓之心，不可不歸建鄴。

translations.literal: At the time many responded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Many responded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 」當時頗相酬許。

translations.literal: After Hongzheng withdrew Huang Luohan and Zong Lin then said, "Hongzheng and Wang Bao are both easterners urging eastward—it is not for the state's plan."
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzheng withdrew Huang Luohan and Zong Lin said, "Hongzheng and Bao are easterners urging east—not for the state."

sentences.zh: 弘正退後，黃羅漢、宗懍乃言：「弘正、王褒並東人，仰勸東下，非為國計」。

translations.literal: Hongzheng secretly knew their words; another day he again faced the emperor and refuted the two, saying, "If easterners urging east is private plan, westerners urging west—is that not also private plan?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng knew their words; another day he refuted them before the emperor: "Easterners urging east is private plan—is westerners urging west not also private?"

sentences.zh: 弘正竊知其言，他日乃復上前面折二人，曰：「若東人勸下東，謂之私計，西人勸住西，亦是私計不？

translations.literal: The crowd was silent and yet sentiment together urged moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd was silent yet sentiment together urged moving the capital.

sentences.zh: 」眾人默然，而人情並勸遷都。

translations.literal: The emperor also once at the rear hall greatly assembled civil and military; those attending were four or five hundred; the emperor wished to test sentiment throughout and said, "Those who urge me to leave bare the left shoulder."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once assembled civil and military at the rear hall—four or five hundred; wishing to test sentiment he said, "Those urging me to leave, bare the left shoulder."

sentences.zh: 上又曾以後堂大集文武，其預會者四五百人，帝欲遍試人情，曰：「勸吾去者左袒。

translations.literal: Thereupon those baring the left shoulder were more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Those baring the left shoulder were more than half.

sentences.zh: 」於是左袒者過半。

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuchang Zhu Maichen was the emperor's old attendant and also a eunuch and fairly capable; therefore the emperor promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang administrator Zhu Maichen was the emperor's old attendant, a eunuch, fairly capable; the emperor promoted him.

sentences.zh: 武昌太守朱買臣，上舊左右，而閹人也，頗有幹用，故上擢之。

translations.literal: At this he urged the emperor to move, saying, "Maichen's home is in Jing Province—would he not wish the ruler to stay long? But I fear it is Maichen's wealth and not the ruler's wealth."
translations.idiomatic: He urged moving: "Maichen's home is Jing—would he not wish the ruler to stay? I fear it is Maichen's wealth, not the ruler's."

sentences.zh: 及是勸上遷，曰：「買臣家在荊州，豈不願官長住，但恐是買臣富貴，非官富貴邪！

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply moved by the words and in the end could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and in the end could not act.

sentences.zh: 」上深感其言，卒不能用。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was especially skilled at arcane speech and also understood Buddhist canon; though great virtuous famous monks none did not ask him to resolve doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng was especially skilled at arcane speech and Buddhist canon; great monks all asked him to resolve doubts.

sentences.zh: 弘正特善玄言，兼明釋典，雖碩德名僧，莫不請質疑滯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in office, aged seventy-nine; posthumously made Attendant and Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died in office, aged seventy-nine; posthumously attendant and director of the Secretariat with posthumous title Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒官，年七十九，贈侍中、中書監，諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: His writings: Zhouyi Lecture and Commentary sixteen scrolls, Lunyu Commentary eleven scrolls, Zhuangzi Commentary eight scrolls, Laozi Commentary five scrolls, Classic of Filial Piety Commentary two scrolls, Collected Writings twenty scrolls—circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His writings: Zhouyi lecture and commentary sixteen scrolls, Lunyu eleven, Zhuangzi eight, Laozi five, Filial Piety two, collected writings twenty—circulated in the age.

sentences.zh: 所著周易講疏十六卷，論語疏十一卷，莊子疏八卷，老子疏五卷，孝經疏二卷，集二十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: Son Yuxuan, aged fourteen, entered the east together in the same carriage; crossing a small boat to shore he saw wisteria flowers; Hongzheng pulled them and the boat overturned and both drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuxuan, fourteen, rode east with him; crossing in a small boat he saw wisteria; Hongzheng pulled and the boat overturned.

sentences.zh: 子豫玄，年十四，與俱載入東，乘小船度岸，見藤花，弘正挽之，船覆俱溺，弘正僅免，豫玄遂得心驚疾。

translations.literal: Hongzheng barely escaped; Yuxuan then got heart-startled illness.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng barely escaped; Yuxuan then got heart-startled illness.

sentences.zh: 次子墳，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Second son Fen, Director of Personnel of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Fen, director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 弘讓性簡素，博學多通。

translations.literal: Hongrang was plain by nature, broadly learned and mastering much.
translations.idiomatic: Hongrang was plain by nature, broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 始仕不得志，隱于句容之茅山，頻征不出。

translations.literal: At first in office he did not succeed and hid on Mount Mao in Jurong; repeatedly summoned he did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At first unsuccessful in office he hid on Mount Mao in Jurong; repeatedly summoned he did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 晚仕侯景，為中書侍郎，人問其故，對曰：「昔王道正直，得以禮進退，今乾坤易位，不至將害於人，吾畏死耳。

translations.literal: Late in office he served Hou Jing as Gentleman of the Secretariat; people asked the reason and he replied, "In the past when the royal way was upright one could advance and withdraw by rites; now heaven and earth have changed place—if one does not arrive one will be harmed by others; I fear death."
translations.idiomatic: Late he served Hou Jing as secretariat gentleman; asked why he replied, "When the royal way was upright one advanced and withdrew by rites; now heaven and earth have changed—if one does not come one is harmed; I fear death."

sentences.zh: 」始彭城劉孝先亦辭辟命，隨兄孝勝在蜀。

translations.literal: At first Pengcheng Liu Xiaoxian also declined appointment and followed elder brother Xiaosheng in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Xiaoxian of Pengcheng also declined appointment and followed elder brother Xiaosheng in Shu.

sentences.zh: 武陵建號，仕為世子府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Wuling declared reign he served as Adviser to the Heir Apparent's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuling declared reign he served as heir-apparent adviser.

sentences.zh: 二隱並獲譏於代。

translations.literal: The two recluses both received censure in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Both recluses received censure in the age.

sentences.zh: 弘讓承聖初，為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the start of Chengsheng Hongrang was Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengsheng's start Hongrang was director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 二年，為仁威將軍，城句容以居之，命曰仁威壘。

translations.literal: In the second year he was General of Benevolent Might, walled Jurong to dwell there, and named it Benevolent Might Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was general of benevolent might, walled Jurong to dwell, and named it Benevolent Might Fort.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉初，以白衣領太常卿、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiancheng in Chen he was in plain clothes concurrent Minister of Ceremonies and Director of Splendid Honors, given gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: At Chen Tiancheng's start he was in plain clothes concurrent minister of ceremonies and director of splendid honors with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 弘讓弟弘直，字思方，幼而聰敏。

translations.literal: Hongrang's younger brother Hongzhi, courtesy name Sifang, was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Hongrang's brother Hongzhi, styled Sifang, was clever from childhood.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為西中郎湘東王外兵記室參軍，與東海鮑泉、南陽宗懍、平原劉緩、沛國劉彀同掌書記。

translations.literal: He served in Liang as Outer Army Recorder under the Western Army Prince of Xiangdong and with Bao Quan of Donghai, Zong Lin of Nanyang, Liu Huan of Pingyuan, and Liu Gu of Pei together managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as outer-army recorder under Prince of Xiangdong and with Bao Quan, Zong Lin, Liu Huan, and Liu Gu managed documents.

sentences.zh: 王出鎮江、荊二州，累除諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the prince went out to garrison the two provinces of Jiang and Jing he was repeatedly promoted to Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince garrisoned Jiang and Jing he rose to adviser.

sentences.zh: 及承制，封湘濱縣侯。

translations.literal: When he received the provisional command he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangbin.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving provisional command he was enfeoffed marquis of Xiangbin.

sentences.zh: 累遷昌州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Chang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to inspector of Chang Province.

sentences.zh: 王琳之舉兵，弘直在湘州，琳敗，乃入陳，位太帝卿、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin raised troops Hongzhi was in Xiang Province; when Lin was defeated he entered Chen and reached Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temple of the Great Emperor and Director of Splendid Honors, given gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin raised troops Hongzhi was in Xiang; when Lin fell he entered Chen and reached minister of the imperial ancestral temple and director of splendid honors with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 弘直方雅敦厚，氣調高於次昆。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was square, elegant, and generous; his tone was higher than the next brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was square, elegant, and generous; his tone higher than the next brother.

sentences.zh: 或問三周孰賢，人曰：「若蜂腰矣」。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Taijian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taijian 7.

sentences.zh: 太建七年卒。

translations.literal: Final instructions: "After breath stops then buy seen timber small in form in the market."
translations.idiomatic: Final instructions: "After breath stops buy small timber seen in the market."

sentences.zh: 遺疏：「氣絕之後，便買市中見材小形者。

translations.literal: Enshroud in timely dress—the ancients' common rule—but descending to meet forebears one must complete rites; one may wear single skirt, robe, shirt, and old shoes."
translations.idiomatic: Enshroud in timely dress—the ancients' rule—but meeting forebears requires full rites: single skirt, robe, shirt, old shoes."

sentences.zh: 斂以時服，古人通制，但下見先人，必須備禮，可著單衣裙衫故履。

translations.literal: Since one should serve in nurture one must prepare veil; or meeting good friends again needs incense smoke; in the coffin only place white cloth hand towel and coarse incense burner—beyond this nothing is used."
translations.idiomatic: For nurture prepare veil; for good friends incense; in the coffin only white cloth towel and coarse incense burner—nothing else."

sentences.zh: 既應侍養，宜備紛帨，或逢善友，又須香煙，棺內唯安白布手巾粗香爐而已，此外無所用。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 」卒於家，年七十六。

translations.literal: Collected writings twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected writings twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: Son Que, courtesy name Shiqian, had beautiful appearance and broad conduct with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Son Que, styled Shiqian, had beautiful appearance and broad integrity.

sentences.zh: 子確，字士潛，美容儀，寬大有行檢。

translations.literal: He ranged through classics and histories and deeply loved arcane speech.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through classics and histories and loved arcane speech.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，篤好玄言。

translations.literal: He reached Director of the Ministry of Justice and died at the start of Zhenming.
translations.idiomatic: He reached director of the ministry of justice and died at Zhenming's start.

sentences.zh: 位都官尚書，禎明初卒。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Literary men do not guard small conduct—ancients and the present are alike in this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Literary men do not guard small conduct—ancients and present alike.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文人不護細行，古令之所同焉。

translations.literal: Because reputation and judgment are known, therefore they give offense to people.
translations.idiomatic: Because reputation and judgment are known, they give offense.

sentences.zh: 由夫聲裁所知，故取忤於人者也。

translations.literal: Looking at Yan and Xie in the Song dynasty—they were not without fame for a generation; Lingyun already met death by it and Yanzhi also stumbled in his year; what was formerly called honoring the person turned into harming oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Xie in Song were famed for a generation; Lingyun died for it and Yanzhi stumbled—the honor they sought became harm.

sentences.zh: 觀夫顏、謝之於宋朝，非不名高一代，靈運既以取斃，延之亦躓當年，向之所謂貴身，翻成害己者矣。

translations.literal: Shixun took brush to count crimes and towered over the foe in difficulty, feeding that kind parent and casting him to the beast's mouth—calling this loyalty, none heard it in former edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun counted crimes with his brush and towered over foes, feeding his kind parent to the beast's mouth—calling that loyalty unheard in former edicts.

sentences.zh: 士遜援筆數罪，陵讎犯難，餌彼慈親，棄之獸吻，以此為忠，無聞前誥。

translations.literal: One who can bear against his own kin will surely bear against others' kin; Shixun forgot his own filiality and hoped to extend others' filiality—unless a stern father's words are fitting and meaning satisfied, it is hard to escape.
translations.idiomatic: One who bears against his own kin will bear against others'; Shixun forgot filiality yet hoped to extend others'—unless a stern father's words fit, escape is hard.

sentences.zh: 夫自忍其親，必將忍人之親，士遜自忘其孝，期以申人之孝，自非嚴父之辭允而義愜，則難乎免矣。

translations.literal: Shibo in conduct indulged desire, loving advance and forgetting retreat—having begun thus he also ended thus; fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo indulged desire, loving advance and forgetting retreat—he began thus and ended thus; fitting.

sentences.zh: 師伯行己縱欲，好進忘退，既以此始，亦以此終，宜乎。

translations.literal: Huaiwen's treading ground was enough to follow ancient exemplars; Confucius's mother feared the censor-in-chief—her warning was deep.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen's tread was enough to follow ancient exemplars; Confucius's mother feared the censor-in-chief—her warning was deep.

sentences.zh: 懷文蹈履之地，足以追蹤古烈，孔母致懼中丞，其誡深矣。

translations.literal: Huaiwen's treading ground was enough to follow ancient exemplars; Confucius's mother feared the censor-in-chief—her warning was deep.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen's tread was enough to follow ancient exemplars; Confucius's mother feared the censor-in-chief—her warning was deep.

sentences.zh: 周朗始終之節，亦倜儻為尤。

translations.literal: Zhou Lang's constancy from beginning to end was also especially free and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang's constancy from start to finish was also especially bold.

sentences.zh: 顒、舍父子，文雅不墜，弘正兄弟義業，幾乎德門者焉。

translations.literal: Yong and She, father and son—the literary elegance did not fall; Hongzheng and his brothers in righteous learning—almost a house of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and She, father and son—literary elegance did not fall; Hongzheng and his brothers in righteous learning—almost a house of virtue.
